It is important to understand the roots of this thinking and the American context. Some decisions are coming from a framework different from the one I knew in the past. events.title: Global private equity investor Advent opens ADGM office
events.summary: Advent, a global private equity investor with more than $109 billion in assets under management, has opened an office in Abu Dhabi’s ADGM , joining the growing list of financial institutions with a presence in the UAE capital. The opening of the new office follows a series of openings by the company globally, including in Tokyo and Hong Kong, the company said in a statement on Wednesday. “The new presence builds on Advent’s long-standing relationships across the Middle East, giving Advent a local base from which to deepen its engagement with investors and support the firm’s existing portfolio companies and explore potential investment opportunities,” the company said. Set up in 1984, the company has made 460 investments in 45 countries. It has 18 offices globally, including in Abu Dhabi. The announcement comes as a growing number of global financial institutions launch their operations at ADGM, despite uncertainty arising from the Iran war. Earlier this month, New Mountain Capital, an alternative investment firm based in New York, said it was opening an office in ADGM to strengthen its presence in the Middle East, while Capital Group, which manages $3.6 trillion in assets, has secured a licence from the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Abu Dhabi's ADGM to operate as a regulated investment manager. The Paris-listed Eurazeo, a European asset manager with €40 billion ($45.2 billion) in assets under management, has also opened an office in the ADGM amid its expansion plans in the region. Other high-profile companies that the UAE capital has attracted in recent months include private credit lender Blue Owl Capital, the tech-focused US company Vista Equity Partners, the world’s largest listed hedge fund Man Group, Barings, Bain Capital, Cantor and the Swiss derivative investment company Adapt Investment Managers. “Advent’s decision to establish an office in ADGM reflects the strength of Abu Dhabi’s proposition as a leading destination for global investment firms,” Arvind Ramamurthy, chief market development officer at ADGM, said. Assets under management at ADGM grew 54 per cent annually in the first six months of 2026, with 49,027 professionals now based at Al Maryah Island and Al Reem Island, an increase of 34 per cent on the same period last year. Collectively, asset managers that established operations in ADGM in the first half of the year oversee more than $2.1 trillion in global assets under management.

events.title: Whoop sees Abu Dhabi as springboard for shift to predictive health, says chief executive
events.summary: Whoop is pushing deeper into the Gulf's longevity economy. The Boston-based human performance company this week announced a clinical research partnership with Abu Dhabi's Department of Health. The deal builds on a $75 million anchor investment from Mubadala Investment Company and a broader buildout that has made the GCC one of Whoop's fastest-growing markets . “This region has become one of the most important regions for Whoop,” its founder and chief executive Will Ahmed tells On the Record with Hadley Gamble . “We're growing extraordinarily fast here in the GCC. We're up about 15 times in the last three years. Our membership base here has grown over 85 per cent just in the past year.” The company has separately put GCC year-on-year growth at more than 75 per cent. Speaking on stage at the Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit , Mr Ahmed said the Department of Health agreement would fund “powerful clinical research to drive health outcomes” around prevention, sleep, cardiovascular health and ageing. The announcement is the latest layer in a multiyear capital and operational push by Abu Dhabi entities into Whoop, which produces wearable health trackers. On May 7, Whoop and Mubadala said they had formed a strategic partnership “to advance proactive health, performance science and preventative healthcare innovation in the UAE”, anchored by the $75 million investment. That investment was made as part of Whoop's $575 million Series G, which valued the company at $10.1 billion. The round was led by Collaborative Fund and, according to the company, included Mubadala and Abu Dhabi-based 2PointZero Group. Under terms disclosed by both sides, Whoop would establish a dedicated office in Abu Dhabi , expand its Advanced Labs blood-testing product, introduce full Arabic localisation across its platform – launched this month with a GCC-wide campaign – and launch the Whoop-Mubadala Health Research Initiative, a longitudinal research programme aimed at strengthening the UAE's health value chain from diagnostics and genomics to prevention and behavioural optimisation. Mr Ahmed has cast the UAE capital as a proving ground for a shift from reactive to predictive care. “The power of continuous health monitoring is that it can really understand signals in your body that you may not be able to feel,” he says. “We believe those insights can actually drive health outcomes, which is to say it can make you lower your weight, it can make you decrease your blood pressure.” He says the company's thesis since its launch 14 years ago – to validate continuous monitoring with elite athletes and then move into the mainstream – is now playing out in the Gulf. He acknowledges the timing, closing a large Gulf investment shortly after the Iran war began, reflects a long-term commitment. “The timing of some of that partnership was complicated with the wars in this region. But to me, it was obvious to show up because I'd been showing up for the last decade,” he says. For Abu Dhabi, the Whoop partnership is one piece of a broader longevity infrastructure play. An EY survey cited by Abu Dhabi officials found only 43 per cent of respondents follow a structured fitness plan, even as 61 per cent had used a wearable in the past year and 87 per cent reported a positive experience using AI for health decisions – a gap officials believe wearables plus clinical integration can close. Whoop, which has now raised about $1 billion in total capital, said the Gulf expansion would be paired with retail distribution, sponsorships with the UAE Team Emirates-XRG cyclists and Al Nassr football team, and, through Whoop Qatar, its first performance research and developement lab outside Boston, later in 2026. “There are many countries in the world that are excited about wearable technology,” Mr Ahmed says. “When you can remove bureaucracy and you can say, look, no, we want health care not to be reactive but actually proactive, then a lot of things fall in suit.”

events.title: Malaysian palm oil drops over 1% on profit-taking
events.summary: The benchmark palm oil contract for January delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange lost RM49. Malaysian palm oil futures fell 1.02% to RM4,768 a tonne on Oct 21, as traders took profits near the top of the trading range. Reuters analyst Wang Tao said prices may fall back to RM4,706-RM4,736 after failing to break resistance at RM4,834. Malaysia’s Oct 1-20 palm oil exports rose 58.5%-78.4% month on month, while higher oil prices could support palm oil demand for biodiesel. JAKARTA – Malaysian palm oil futures fell more than 1% on Oct 21 , with profit-taking near the top of the trading range outweighing gains in rival vegetable oils on the Dalian Commodity Exchange. The benchmark palm oil contract for January delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange lost RM49 (S$15), or 1.02%, to RM4,768 a metric ton at the close. “Prices retreated on profit-taking as they hovered near the upper end of the trading range,” a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said. Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract rose 0.26%, while its palm oil contract climbed 1.31%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were down 0.12%. Palm oil tracks rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market. Cargo surveyors estimated that Malaysian palm oil products exports for Oct 1-20 rose between 58.5% and 78.4% from a month earlier. Oil prices rose by more than US$1 on Oct 21 as attacks on Gulf shipping and no signs of diplomatic progress to end the Iran war fuelled supply disruption fears, with the Brent benchmark hovering near 5-month highs, while falling US crude and product inventories also lent support to the market. events.title: Bereaved civil service families could face ‘unjust’ tax bills due to pension scheme delays
events.summary: MPs say ‘chaos’ at Capita-run scheme could mean some claims miss tax-free time limit on lump sum payments Bereaved families could face “unconscionable” tax bills because of “chaos” in the civil service pension scheme, the government has been warned. Some lump sum pension payments to families are only tax-free if made within two years of a scheme being told of the member’s death. MPs are now voicing fears that severe delays in the administration of the civil service pension scheme, which is run by the outsourcing company Capita , could push some families over that threshold. They would then be hit with a tax bill calculated at the recipient’s personal rate. The families of more than 1,600 deceased civil servants have been waiting for more than 100 days for their “death in benefit” claim to be processed, according to the latest figures . Some of those have reported struggling to pay bills because of the delay. The Conservative MP Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, who chairs the Commons public accounts committee (PAC), said: “The chaos currently engulfing the civil service pensions scheme means that the likelihood of death benefit payments being made within two years is slim.” He added: “It is unconscionable that the families of loyal and dedicated civil servants, who are continuing to suffer through this serious government failing, could potentially face such an unjust financial penalty.” The Cabinet Office, which is responsible for the pension scheme, said it was unable to prevent HM Revenue and Customs from taxing delayed claims, and that affected members would have to claw back the money by taking their case to the Pensions Ombudsman. The ombudsman estimates an 18-month wait to resolve cases because of the volume of complaints from those affected. The PAC has called for a change in legislation to prevent relatives paying the price for administrative delays. The government has already been accused of letting down civil servants and their families by repeatedly outsourcing the 1.7-million-member pension scheme to private companies that failed to deliver. The PAC last year urged ministers to take the scheme in-house after a previous contractor, MyCSP, was blamed for plummeting service levels. However, the £239m contract passed to Capita last December, despite concerns voiced by some that the company was inadequately prepared. The Cabinet Office said it was confident that Capita would offer an improved service. It has since acknowledged that service levels were “unacceptable”. MyCSP and Capita were contacted for a comment. In February, a dedicated email address was set up for unions to escalate cases of severe hardship caused by the delays. The cases referred included claimants at risk of suicide or of losing their homes. Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning Clare Norris has been waiting 11 months for the death benefit and pension payments she is due after her husband died last November. “I was petrified – I am 52 and early death was not part of our financial plan,” she said. “Losing your partner is one of the most difficult experiences anyone can go through. The lack of clarity, communication and basic administrative handling from Civil Service Pensions has made it considerably worse.” Capita said her case would be progressed under a new process. “It remains a high priority and the member can expect to hear on next steps as soon as possible.” Under HMRC rules, in cases in which someone dies under the age of 75, tax-free lump sum payments must be made within two years, otherwise they will be taxed at the recipient’s marginal rate of tax. The Cabinet Office said it was committed to ensuring scheme members were not left out of pocket. “We are continuing to hold Capita to account, including holding back nearly £10m in payments, and are doing everything in our power to ensure individuals do not experience delays,” said a spokesperson. “If delays cause a tax charge, existing avenues for complaints can provide financial redress or compensation to cover losses.”

events.title: Stratford International on track to get cross-Channel trains in budget boost
events.summary: Sadiq Khan says upgrade would unlock station’s true potential and allow it to live up to its name Stratford International train station in east London will receive funding in next week’s budget, according to reports, putting it on track to live up to its name and become a hub for cross-Channel services. London’s mayor, Sadiq Khan, has been making a case to ministers for funding to upgrade the station to allow it to start running international rail services. Until now only domestic routes running to and from central London and Kent have stopped at the station, although Eurostar services pass through on the way to and from St Pancras. Khan said: “We’ve been working closely with the government to make Stratford International truly ‘international’ for the first time – opening up new opportunities for jobs, investment and tourism, while connecting one of the UK’s fastest-growing economic centres directly to Europe. “It’s time to unlock the full potential of this station and help write the next chapter in Stratford’s remarkable success story.” Khan recently argued that growth in international rail travel and environmental concerns meant it would be better to improve Stratford International than expand Heathrow airport by building a third runway. Stratford International would require a significant upgrade from its current two platforms to allow it to welcome international services, including adding a border post and security checks as well as a check-in zone, waiting area and facilities for passengers. The work opening up the station and the mothballed international section of the station, including platforms and a waiting area, would cost an estimated £20m , according to the Standard. It reported Khan’s plan was for one in three trains to and from France to stop at the station, while it could also become a hub for rail services from the continent to the Midlands and the north of England. The station, located close to the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, opened in late 2009 and was originally designed and built with the intention of handling Eurostar trains, but this was not fully developed. The chancellor, John Healey, is reportedly planning to greenlight the mayor’s proposal to create a business rate retention zone, according to the Financial Times, to help fund the station’s redevelopment. Such zones allow local authorities to keep all of the businesses rates growth collected in their area – rather than half of the rates collected, as is standard – to fund local regeneration directly. Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning In recent months, Virgin and other rail companies have been in talks with City Hall about operating future international rail services from Stratford. Virgin is planning to launch rail services from London to the continent in 2030, bringing direct competition to Eurostar on the cross-Channel route for the first time since the opening of the tunnel. The operator has been granted access by the rail regulator to the track and to Eurostar’s nearby Temple Mills depot . A spokesperson for the Virgin Group said the operator was “looking forward to exploring additional stops, including Stratford International”. They added that the company had been “actively engaging with stakeholders to explore future expansion” beyond its initial launch plans. Gemini Trains, chaired by the Labour peer Tony Berkeley, is hoping to run trains to France, Belgium and Germany and has said it wanted to use Stratford as its London hub. However, it has not yet been granted depot and track access.

events.title: Bringing the Spark to Europe: Local Intelligence Powers Next Wave of Agents
events.summary: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing its full lineup of local AI hardware. RTX Spark , which launched last week , powers personal agents on Windows PCs; DGX Spark supports developers building and scaling applications on Linux; and DGX Station serves enterprise teams running frontier workloads on Linux, with a Windows version arriving in December. Underdog Desktop Agent now available for RTX Spark DGX Spark 64GB available on Friday, Oct. 23 NVIDIA Sync to support eight DGX Sparks and add Model Launcher this month October DGX Spark software update adds Wi-Fi Assistant and updates DGX Spark Skills DGX Station improves manageability with seven new integrations DGX Station for Windows launches in December with support for many manufacturing apps and agent harnesses Three new open source reference workflows for robotics on DGX Station NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to DGX Station Recursive Flint, a new local coding model, is now available for NVIDIA local hardware Day-0 support for new Nemotron, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and FLUX.3 AI models New accelerations for llama.cpp and vLLM inference engines and a new collection of checkpoints optimized for local AI hardware. Learn more about these local AI announcements below, and check out the demos and sessions at GTC Berlin . RTX Spark Brings Personal Agents to the Windows PC RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — running personal agents, accelerated content creation and 1440p 100 frames-per-second gaming with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute. Here’s what early reviewers are saying about the platform since its October 16 release: “A dream machine for serious creators … ” — CGMag “Designed for the future of AI … ” — The Verge “An extremely capable, surprisingly portable and efficient machine … ” — PCMag Underdog , a new desktop agent app built for fully local, private AI, is also bringing its experience to RTX Spark. Powered by its Husky model-specific inference engine, Underdog runs models entirely on device, so personal agents can get work done without user data ever leaving the PC. Underdog is available now for download . To better enable developers and enthusiasts to build and customize local agents, many RTX Spark laptops come with an unlocked bootloader. During the GTC keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed off how AI agents running on RTX Spark can be used to train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B. ASUS, Dell Technologies , HP , Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI laptops are available today, with Acer coming soon. Learn more about RTX Spark , and get started with the latest RTX Spark playbooks . DGX Spark Gives Developers Room to Build New DGX Spark 64GB systems — that can run models including Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B 24GB, Qwen3.8 27B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B — start rolling out from partners on Friday, Oct. 23. When workloads require more capacity, developers can connect multiple DGX Spark systems via built-in NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant . This allows users to run advanced coding models like Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, DeepSeek v4 Flash 0731 and GLM 5.3 Flash. Now, DGX Spark supports clusters of up to eight units in manual configuration, enabling larger models, longer contexts, concurrent agents and distributed development. Ideal for small teams sharing a single cluster as a backend, with each developer running concurrent sessions against the same model, it delivers 1TB of unified memory — enough to run frontier-class models like GLM 5.3. Get started with the DGX Spark cluster playbook . NVIDIA Sync Model Launcher will also be available later this month. It simplifies access to local AI on a single DGX Spark or a cluster. With a few clicks, Model Launcher downloads a model and container suited to the configuration and connects the model to OpenCode. It automatically loads DGX Spark Skills for troubleshooting, device maintenance, access to official documentation and other workflow guidance. The October DGX Spark software update brings a new Wi-Fi Assistant that lets users switch networks when DGX Spark is running in appliance mode. Plus, DGX Spark Skills provide workflow-focused guidance in troubleshooting and device maintenance directly into NVIDIA Sync via OpenCode. DGX Spark systems are available directly from Acer , ASUS , Dell Technologies , GIGABYTE , HP , Lenovo, MSI and NVIDIA. DGX Station Puts Frontier Intelligence at the Desk For larger teams, DGX Station offers 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of AI performance, enabling developers to run advanced models like GLM 5.3 and serve 30+ users at speeds comparable to those provided by cloud models. Adding scale, NVIDIA Sync now supports DGX Station, simplifying connections between two Linux-based systems. New integrations with Absolute Security , Splunk by Cisco , Fleet Device Managemen t , Microsoft Intune , Perforce Puppet , Progress Software Chef and Tanium let IT teams manage DGX Station systems through enterprise setup, management and conformity processes, helping accelerate approvals and reduce deployment risk while minimizing time to first token. With the upcoming Windows-based systems, developers can build workflows that harness professional applications, run on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs and operate from agents that run their large language models (LLMs) on NVIDIA GB300 systems — all in one machine. DGX Station for Windows , expected from system manufacturer partners in December, extends local AI into the applications and operating environment enterprises already use. Engineers can run local models and agents in Windows-native software with access to AI models, tools and agents on the same system. DGX Station for Windows will feature support for manufacturing applications from nTop , Dassault Systèmes , Keysight Technologies , MathWorks , Rockwell Automation , Siemens , Synopsys , Unity and Altera for AI-guided design, simulation, validation and engineering automation. Users will be able to run agents using Hermes Agent , Perplexity or Aible on premises for agentic control in enterprise environments. The same local, controlled computing model extends to robotics. DGX Station gives robotics teams dedicated compute for post-training, simulation and evaluation, shortening iteration cycles without waiting for shared infrastructure. Developers can use them to refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills and post-train Cosmos world models for synthetic data generation. events.title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure
events.summary: General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. Learning through interaction requires a continuous cycle of generating experience, evaluating outcomes and updating models, requiring infrastructure that can support the entire process at scale. A5X brings Vera Rubin into Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer as an integrated system, combining compute, networking and storage to support experience-driven learning at scale. “We’re building superlearners that continually improve through their own experience,” said David Silver, founder and CEO of Ineffable Intelligence. “That demands both substantial compute and a tight connection between generating experience and training on it, so each improvement in the agent can quickly shape its next experience. Vera Rubin’s combination of compute performance and high-bandwidth connectivity, between the Vera CPU and Rubin GPUs and between the Rubin GPUs within the rack, allow us to push the scale and ambition of our reinforcement learning research further.” WPP , a London-based marketing and communications company, has also demonstrated its creative agent reference architecture on NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based A5X instances using NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA OpenShell, part of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for safe AI agents. The agents turn conversational requests into multistep creative workflows, such as video generation, upscaling and restyling, with human approval before execution. OpenShell provides governed sandboxes for agent execution, helping control access to sensitive brand assets and creative tools. In WPP’s initial tests, workloads that typically required a multi-node cluster ran on a single A5X instance. As organizations deploy agentic systems, they need to protect the proprietary models and sensitive data that power these systems — even when running on infrastructure they don’t own. Google Cloud will be among the first cloud providers to offer NVIDIA Confidential Computing at rack scale on bare metal instances such as A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Additionally, Google Cloud is making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, offering a flexible platform for confidential inference and fine-tuning. Customers including Vertebrae , Polaris Cloud and Confidential Core AI are using Confidential G4 for conversational privacy, verifiable agent execution and policy-governed enterprise intelligence. To support energy-efficient deployment at scale, Google Cloud and NVIDIA are exploring NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS capabilities for Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to help optimize performance per watt and expand capacity within available data-center power budgets. Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Google Cloud A5X instances. events.title: Former chief executive banned after misconduct led to £4m losses in high-risk investments
events.summary: The FCA has banned Jeffrey Dawkins, the former chief executive of Vector Wealth Ltd, after he dishonestly acted as a front for a disqualified director using the company to sell high-risk bonds. Mr Dawkins has also been fined nearly £270,000.In 2019, Mr Dawkins sold Vector Wealth to a disqualified director who described himself as CEO and wanted to use Vector Wealth’s FCA-authorised status to sell mini-bonds.Mr Dawkins told the FCA he was still in charge, but the new “CEO” was really running the firm. This deception allowed the disqualified director to promote mini-bonds using the legitimacy of the firm to make them appear safer than they were.The disqualified director and Kadir Kanizi, a former senior manager at Vector Wealth, promoted the bonds but investors were not properly warned about the risks.Investors put in £105,000 on average, with one investing £1.1 million. Before seeing the marketing material, they had to confirm they were high net worth or sophisticated investors. Investors are expected to lose about £4 million.The FCA has banned Mr Kanizi from senior management roles. He was fined for failing to make sure consumers were properly warned about the risks.Therese Chambers, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said, 'Jeffrey Dawkins acted as a front man for a banned director, helping high-risk investments look safer than they were.'Mr Dawkins and Mr Kanizi allowed misleading promotions to draw in investors, many of whom now face significant losses. Mini-bonds and similar investments are very high risk, and people should be extremely cautious.'The FCA has warned about the risks of investing in mini-bonds and loan notes. A loan note or mini-bond usually involves lending money to a company for a set period in return for interest. If that company fails, consumers could lose every penny.Consumers need to be alert to the risk of harm and protect themselves using the tools available, like the FCA Firm Checker.Notes to editorsRead the final notices for Jeffrey Dawkins and Kadir Kanizi.There is statutory obligation to report the change in control of authorised firms.Vector Wealth Limited was formed as Fifth Quarter Asset Management (UK) Limited on 23 March 2012. Mr Dawkins held authorised positions at the firm from 5 March 2013. Vector Wealth’s authorisation ended on 28 January 2025.Mr Kanizi was appointed as a director on 22 September 2020 and was approved by the FCA on 6 September 2021.The disqualified director was banned from acting as a company director for 12 years in August 2014.The penalty in respect of Mr Dawkins includes a multiplier to reflect the seriousness of the conduct. It also includes an uplift for failing to cooperate with the FCA’s investigation. The full calculation is set out at section 6 of the Final Notice. Mr Dawkins has also been ordered to pay £57,298 plus interest (£68,257) of the proceeds he received from selling Vector Wealth and continuing to act as its director and approved person.The FCA has calculated that Kadir Kanizi should have been fined £80,096 but it reduced the penalty to £20,000 after he demonstrated that it would cause serious financial hardship. In the interest of maximising the funds available to be distributed to investors, the FCA agreed not to enforce the penalty if the same amount was made available by Mr Kanizi to Vector Wealth’s liquidators. He has also agreed to complete consumer duty training before taking up any future role in financial services.Investors who bought bonds through Vector Wealth should contact the firm’s liquidator and check the FCA website for updates.The FCA has investigated the matters that fall within its remit. The FCA may share relevant information with other law enforcement agencies where appropriate. Confirming or comment on individual referrals could risk affecting ongoing investigations.The FCA now actively removes the unutilised permissions of firms. Historically firms were expected to voluntarily request cancellation of unused permissions.The FCA permanently banned the marketing of speculative illiquid securities, including mini-bonds and loan notes, to retail investors from 1 January 2021.Anyone approached about loan notes, mini-bonds or similar high-risk investments should stop and check before investing, especially where adverts promise big, fixed returns or make the investment look simple and safe. Use the FCA’s Firm Checker and Warning List before handing over any money.

events.title: NVIDIA and Supply Chain Partners Expand Capacity to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Buildout
events.summary: Substrate agreements with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corporation will, in aggregate, drive a 2.5x increase in capacity over the next three years. Amkor plans to increase its advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028. KYEC will build new facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. SPIL is targeting to increase its optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform. Working with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation, NVIDIA is enabling new and existing suppliers to expand critical manufacturing capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines, strengthening the resiliency and redundancy of NVIDIA’s global supply chain. “We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.” Expanding Substrate Capacity to Support Volume Growth NVIDIA plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. The agreements below will contribute to this capacity expansion, with more underway. Under an agreement signed and announced earlier this year by IBIDEN, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN’s Ono Plant in Japan. The expansion targets capacity reaching 3x current levels at the plant, with additional capacity expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining NVIDIA’s substrate supply chain, bringing immediate capacity from its existing operations in South Korea. The collaboration also supports facility upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, production allocated to NVIDIA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total annual package substrate production capacity. NVIDIA is supporting Unimicron’s KF substrate manufacturing expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation agreement. The expansion is expected to begin adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028. Scaling Advanced Packaging for Next-Generation Platforms NVIDIA and Amkor plan to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, targeting a greater than 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028. The planned capacity expansion, alongside Amkor’s development of new manufacturing facilities in South Korea, will support higher production volumes for NVIDIA’s current and next-generation platforms. Expanding Semiconductor Testing and Strengthening US Manufacturing NVIDIA expects its total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, supported by buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan and Singapore. NVIDIA’s $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027. In Singapore, expanded testing operations are expected to begin high-volume production in February 2027. Creating the Infrastructure for Co-Packaged Optics NVIDIA and SPIL plan to expand manufacturing capacity in Taiwan for optical engines used in co-packaged optics, supporting the growing connectivity requirements of large-scale computing infrastructure. The expansion targets an increase of 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. About NVIDIA NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI and accelerated computing. events.title: Giant tunnel proposed to tackle Windermere sewage discharges
events.summary: United Utilities, Environment Agency and local campaigners say 12-mile tunnel could take sewage away from England’s largest lake Plans are under way for a new giant tunnel to transport sewage away from Windermere, England’s largest lake. Windermere, in the Lake District, has suffered from widespread raw sewage and bacterial pollution driven by discharges from United Utilities . Campaigners say this pollution has caused more frequent toxic blue-green algal blooms, with the public advised to avoid swimming in the lake. Modelling indicates the climate crisis will exacerbate these challenges, with the catchment expected to experience more intense rainfall over the coming years, placing further pressure on the wastewater infrastructure. A new project, backed by United Utilities, the Environment Agency and local campaigners, has set out a vision to end sewage discharges into the lake by building an 12-mile (19km) tunnel to transport sewage away from the lake. The water company said the use of tunnelling techniques would minimise the disruption to local communities. Windermere is at the heart of the Lake District Unesco world heritage site and has been the inspiration for poets, storytellers and lyricists for generations, with an estimated 17.7 million people visiting every year. The treated effluent would then be discharged into either the River Leven or the Irish Sea at Ulverston. It is estimated the project will cost £3.6bn, with United Utilities to seek permission from the government to raise customer bills to pay for it. It said the programme could add up to £3.17 a month to water bills in 2035. The project will now enter the detailed design phase during which specialised engineers will work out the technicalities of the build, which is expected to take two years. If granted permission to raise bills to pay for the project, United Utilities said the project could be complete within seven years and would provide a “one and done” solution with an immediate impact. The planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential Matt Staniek, a campaigner at Save Windermere, which is a partner on the project, said creating the feasibility report had involved weekly meetings over 15 months. Staniek, who has been calling for the end of sewage discharges into the lake for more than five years, said he was concerned at first about partnering with the company causing the pollution, but said they were the only people who could actually fix it. “This has demonstrated that it is possible not to dump sewage in Lake Windermere,” he said. In planning for the project, the team considered the transformation of Lake Annecy in France, which is widely recognised as one of the cleanest lakes in Europe. In the 1950s, Annecy faced similar pollution problems, but the authorities invested in long-term infrastructural improvements to eliminate the sewage discharges. “This is up to the government now. The plan is there, it’s in place, we’re not going to stop until Andy Burnham is on the shores of Lake Windermere with a spade announcing that the construction has begun on this project,” Staniek said.

events.title: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents
events.summary: Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful. Aleria, Cassava Technologies , Firebird , G42 , Radiant, SWI Compute and Vultr are also developing and expanding NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia. Regional capacity from AI clouds combines the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform , including NVIDIA Vera Rubin, NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, giving customers greater choice and control over where workloads and data reside while advancing sovereign computing services and economic growth. Open: Models and Libraries, From Training to Inference Across the ecosystem, AI clouds are expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and services for developers to build applications with open models and libraries. This new capacity supports model training, fine-tuning for specialized tasks and inference at scale, including applications deployed at the edge. For production inference, Nebius has adopted NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, using Spectrum-X Ethernet networking to integrate it with Vera Rubin NVL72 on Nebius Token Factory. The combination will bring faster token generation to latency-sensitive applications and agentic systems through the platform’s managed serverless and dedicated endpoints and familiar application programming interfaces. For robotics and physical AI, Nebius offers a purpose-built AI cloud solution that includes its full-stack Physical AI Workbench. Robotics companies including Rhoda AI , RoboForce and Sereact are building on the platform. The company also launched three NVIDIA retail agent blueprints — covering inventory, store operations, and fine-tuning —- into early access on Nebius infrastructure. Nebius is expanding its cloud services widely across the continent with its Physical AI Living Lab, and in Germany as a computer supplier for the Next Frontier Challenge of SPRIND, the Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation. Baseten has developed a specialized model for code-review routing with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning used by CodeRabbit. Through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, CodeRabbit improved routing agreement from 75.8% to 80.7% while reducing estimated inference costs by 50% for the evaluated workload. The results demonstrate how AI developers can customize NVIDIA open models for specialized tasks while improving accuracy and inference efficiency. Fireworks and Era4 are partnering to bring open models to enterprises across the U.K. and Europe. The collaboration combines Fireworks ’ model training and inference platform with direct liquid-cooled capacity powered by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs at Era4’s Chesterfield facility, supporting plans for enterprise AI solutions in financial services, insurance and life sciences. Mistral is expanding its NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure to support model training, customization and inference. The expansion includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure planned for delivery in 2027. Trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral -operated European data centers, Mistral Large 4 is the company’s latest frontier multimodal model, advancing capabilities across coding, agentic workflows and multimodal understanding. Verda plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin, continuing to promote open weight models with NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos already in production, and using the NVIDIA Dynamo open source framework for inference optimization. Safe: Secure Boundaries for AI Agents, From Silicon to Software As developers connect models to tools and business systems, they also need controls over what agents can access and do. Announced at GTC Berlin, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture with support from AI cloud ecosystem partners. Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture is designed to give organizations full-stack control to deploy AI agents with clear boundaries around what agents can access and do. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs with OpenShell for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. Each play a distinct role in delivering that control, working together so agents can achieve what they’re meant to do without moving beyond the boundaries people set for them. Partners including Aleria , Baseten , Cassava , CoreWeave , Crusoe , DigitalOcean , Firebird , Fireworks, Firmus , G42 , GMI Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Lightning AI, Nebius , Nscale , Radiant Verda and Vultr are supporting the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enable secure agentic deployments for their customers. Together, European AI clouds are connecting regional infrastructure investment with the work of building and deploying AI. Expanded capacity gives builders more places to run workloads.

events.title: Europe’s Industrial Leaders Reinvent Engineering and Manufacturing With NVIDIA
events.summary: To increase productivity, accelerate innovation and create new opportunities for economic growth, Europe’s industrial leaders are tapping NVIDIA CUDA-X and Omniverse libraries , as well as NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron open models, across the engineering and manufacturing lifecycle. Bringing those capabilities together on the factory floor, the NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) is now available in early access on GitHub , providing a path for developers to build and deploy always-on factory manager agents that coordinate work across machines, and specialist agents focused on use cases such as visual inspection, root cause analysis, report generation and fleet management. These agents can connect to frontier models, including NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron, and foundational knowledge including computer-aided design, product lifecycle management, simulation software, and IT and operational technology systems. Building on the FOX blueprint enables the ecosystem to build industrial agents that monitor factory operations in real time, correlate visual findings and machine logs to investigate problems, and coordinate responses. With Cosmos in-context learning, these agents can adapt using examples and documentation, without fine-tuning. Siemens is integrating agents built using FOX into Intelligence Center X, its agentic enterprise system, to help identify root causes and coordinate factory operations, for estimated cost savings of 20%. Siemens’ Process Preparation X agents use NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory tools and skills to generate defect images for circuit-board inspection. At its Erlangen electronics factory, Siemens used this approach to reduce calibration time of inspection processes by 40%. Accelerating Engineering From the First Design NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries accelerate simulation, giving engineers faster feedback to explore design alternatives before committing to physical prototypes. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is releasing cuDSS for general availability , accelerating the demanding calculations behind the complex simulations of structural stress, fluid flow, electromagnetic fields and semiconductor device behavior. Mercedes-Benz uses Siemens’ Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on NVIDIA GPUs to compare vehicle designs through faster aerodynamic simulations. In factories, the company applies NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and the Metropolis VSS blueprint to build agents for vehicle inspection and windshield assembly verification, detecting deviations and ensuring consistently high quality. Cadence is benchmarking automotive fluid-dynamics workloads on NVIDIA GPUs to assess opportunities for faster design iteration, while Autodesk brings the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and Warp frameworks into NavPack, integrated with Autodesk Alias, to help designers like those at Bentley’s predict vehicle performance and iterate faster using simulation-trained AI. imec and Infineon are accelerating semiconductor simulation with Synopsys software and NVIDIA accelerated computing. Benchmarks of S-Litho on imec’s model show up to 40x speedup, while Infineon uses Sentaurus Device with NVIDIA CUDA libraries to achieve a 12x speedup in 3D breakdown simulation for next-generation power devices. Leonardo is working with Neural Concept on AI-driven aircraft design, tapping NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bring aircraft geometry and aerodynamic simulation results together. Car manufacturers use Dassault Systèmes ’ LEO & AURA Virtual Companions, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, and orchestrating CATIA AI Agents & SIMULIA AI Agents with SIMULIA solvers, accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, to rapidly design and virtually test vehicle doors before building physical prototypes. UniversalAGI is working with Saab to protect sailors from life-threatending wave impacts at sea, using UniversalAGI’s Latent Interaction Field Transformer physics AI foundation models with accelerated processing by NVIDIA Warp to evaluate thousands of wave conditions and headings in real time instead of days. These capabilities enable vessels to anticipate dangerous motion and autonomously select safer routes to avoid putting sailors at risk, while NVIDIA Omniverse libraries help visualize vessel behavior at sea. PhysicsX is working with GB1, Britain’s America’s Cup team , on AI-powered yacht design, using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to visualize hull geometry and pressure fields, while Fermioniq ’s Sofia agent helps Deltares and Dutch ministries model river flow by translating natural-language requests into simulation solvers built on NVIDIA Warp. Mistral plans to use CUDA-X, Warp and Omniverse libraries to accelerate physics simulation and generate training data for engineering AI models. Testing Factories and Robots Virtually NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac libraries enable digital twins and robotics simulation , helping manufacturers evaluate production systems and robot behavior before making changes on the factory floor. Audi uses a battery-production digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to test production concepts before physical equipment is available. The company is also working with Dassault Systèmes and Agile Robots to simulate and validate mobile humanoid robots and logistics processes in DELMIA virtual twins built with Omniverse libraries. Schaeffler is integrating digital twins of its humanoid actuators — components that move robot joints — with NVIDIA Isaac simulation frameworks, helping its robotics partners evaluate component behavior in simulation and reduce physical testing. At Volkswagen Sachsen’s Transparent Factory, Wandelbots uses NOVA with Isaac Sim , built on Omniverse and OpenUSD, to validate assembly workflows digitally and prepare applications for physical robots. Falkor , a KONGSBERG company, is integrating agents and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries into its platform. With Microsoft Azure NCv6 virtual machines powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, agents with spatial intelligence combine engineering data, operating information and 3D equipment geometry to see, simulate and reason over industrial facilities, supporting inspection and maintenance use cases across the process and energy industries. The same simulation approach extends to AI infrastructure. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA , is developing an AI factory digital twin built for Nscale with Omniverse libraries to help engineers compare power, cooling and equipment configurations before making physical changes. events.title: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations
events.summary: NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an NVIDIA CUDA-X library that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs. Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test. NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost. Industry leaders are already integrating NVIDIA cuDSS into their tools to transform workflows for their end customers: Applied Materials: With cuDSS, Applied Materials accelerated sparse solves in Ginestra, its physics-based, defect-centric simulation platform, by up to 10x versus CPU-only approaches, speeding exploration of semiconductor materials and device reliability. COMSOL: Using COMSOL Multiphysics with NVIDIA cuDSS on NVIDIA accelerated computing, ZEISS SMT achieved a measured 4x speedup in an EUV lithography plasma simulation benchmark, completing the full simulation in six days and 14 hours. Cadence : Uses cuDSS in its Celsius software to accelerate simulations of heat, structural stress and warpage in advanced chips and 3D chip designs, helping customers including Nokia analyze complex designs faster. Dassault Systèmes : Dassault Systèmes reports an 8-10x speedup using cuDSS within its Abaqus structural and computer simulation technology electromagnetic solvers for performance-critical simulations across industries. Siemens : Siemens uses cuDSS in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to accelerate simulations of structures in fluid-structure interaction workflows. Synopsys : Synopsys uses cuDSS in its Sentaurus Device simulator tool to accelerate simulations of advanced logic, memory and power chips, helping Infineon model increasingly complex devices faster. As simulation workloads grow in size and complexity, cuDSS can scale out of the box from individual workstations to large computing clusters. Developers can integrate cuDSS into existing engineering, scientific and optimization software offerings, bringing GPU acceleration to tools already used by engineers and researchers. They can use cuDSS through C, C++, Python and Fortran interfaces. Learn more about cuDSS by visiting the NVIDIA demo booth and Dassault Systèmes booth at GTC Berlin. events.title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure
events.summary: NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents across the stack . The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced today , is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running. Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data. NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure. NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options: Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories. Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide. Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution. “Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.” Google Cloud is extending support for Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property. “Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud. Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution. Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems. CoreWeave , Firmus , GMI Cloud , Google Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Microsoft Azure Infrastructure, Nebius , Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. Global systems partners including Cisco , Dell Technologies , HPE , Lenovo, Supermicro and Bull will support these capabilities with NVIDIA-Certified Systems . NVIDIA DSX OS will support all NVIDIA Confidential Computing modes, giving cloud providers a software foundation for building and operating AI factories that support confidential workloads. events.title: Faisal Islam: Inflation and borrowing figures illustrate chancellor's Budget challenge
events.summary: Published 21 October 2026, 11:03 BST The chancellor was on an early flight to North East Scotland on Wednesday to announce new North Sea energy approvals as the last set of major economic figures dropped. From a mile high, as well as close up, the figures for inflation and for the public finances set out his Budget balancing act in clear terms. The National Debt has topped £3 trillion for the first time in the official figures. The headline rate of inflation has hit 3.5% and is surely heading back up to 4% in the coming months. Borrowing is running ahead of forecasts, as spending and interest costs increase. These show the constraints for John Healey as he puts the finishing touches to his statement next week. On the one hand he says he wants to give "breathing space" to consumers yet again feeling the heat from cost of living pressures. The public finances remain under pressure, however, from the double whammy of rising inflation and borrowing costs. While inflation was of course expected to increase as petrol and diesel prices surged, in some cases, to records, other measures of underlying inflation also increased. From airfares to computer game download prices, there are the first signs of stickier forms of price pressure and of higher inflation becoming more embedded, suggesting elevated price rises are not temporary. Capital Economics now expects the main measure of inflation to peak at 4.2% next year. The Bank of England carefully watches services inflation and core inflation, and this ups the odds significantly for a rise in interest rates next month. The services sector, which includes everything from law and banking to retail, hospitality and tourism, makes up the vast majority of the UK's economic output. The latest inflation figure also applies as the uprating to tens of billions in welfare payments next April. By law, benefits such as personal independence payment (PIP) and carer's allowance must rise in line with September's consumer price index (CPI) measure of inflation. The figure also confirms that the Triple Lock will see the State Pension increase by 3.9% next April. There is one form of relief here - food price inflation remains largely unaffected by the energy shock. While higher inflation at a time of frozen tax thresholds will raise more tax in cash terms, it will also increase the cost of public services, including likely union pay demands. All the while, UK borrowing costs have risen alongside most of the advanced world as the US-Israel war against Iran has intensified. The Jackdaw gas field decision is seen as the start of a run of "pro growth" pre-Budget announcements. It sends a directional message, but will not fundamentally change the trade off between cost of living breathing space, and delivering a Budget that convinces the markets and investors. The fact the borrowing costs gap has narrowed a bit with other G7 nations, and the IMF praised pencilled-in plans to shrink borrowing, provided a platform for the chancellor's Budget. The latest economic numbers amply illustrate the challenge of actually delivering them. events.title: NVIDIA Advances Isaac Platform for General-Purpose Robotics With New Reference Humanoid, Frameworks, Simulation Pipelines and Data
events.summary: News Summary:  Agile Robots announces Agile ONE SN, a humanoid reference platform built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and NVIDIA Jetson Thor with planned integration of the NVIDIA Halos safety stack, giving developers and researchers a complete platform for frontier humanoid development and validation. NVIDIA Isaac platform adds new Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0 for robot learning and open source reference workflows that combine ChatGPT Astra with NVIDIA Isaac and Cosmos on NVIDIA DGX Station to accelerate robot data generation, training and evaluation. Europe’s robotics ecosystem, including leaders like ABB Robotics, Flexion, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Sereact and Universal Robots, is building on NVIDIA’s open robotics platform to advance autonomous robotic systems.    GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced a major expansion of the NVIDIA Isaac™ open robotics development platform , adding a reference humanoid, datasets and runtime, along with updates to its robot learning framework. Together, these technologies give developers an integrated path from data to deployment to bring general-purpose robots to the real-world faster. “General-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed — the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA Isaac, our full-stack open robotics platform, we are giving developers the models, data, simulation tools and computing systems to bring physical AI to the world’s largest industries.” Agile ONE SN — A Frontier Humanoid Reference Platform for Research Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN , a full-stack reference humanoid preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and powered by the NVIDIA Jetson Thor ™ edge AI platform. Robotics researchers and developers often struggle to integrate the separate simulation, training and deployment tools needed to take robot skills from development to the physical world. Agile ONE SN unifies these tools and workflows on a single platform, cutting setup time from weeks to days. Agile ONE SN features: Agile ONE S humanoid body, standing 1.40 meters (4.59 feet tall) and weighing 40 kilograms (88 pounds), with 31 degrees of freedom and a 3-kilogram payload per arm. Dual WUJI Hand 2 five-finger hands, each offering 20 degrees of freedom, 1kHz force control and tactile sensing for dexterous manipulation NVIDIA Jetson Thor onboard compute, delivering 2,070 FP4 teraflops of compute and 128GB of unified memory for onboard reasoning and real-time control. Multimodal sensing , including head and wrist cameras, lidar sensors and inertial measurement units to help the robot perceive and interact with its surroundings. NVIDIA Isaac GR00T platform, which comprises the GR00T foundation model, a full workflow from data capture to deployment and whole-body control for coordinated movement. Safety capabilities, with planned integration of on-robot safety protocols with the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system for robotics.   “The breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale: one adaptable machine that learns many skills and works across environments built for people,” said Zhaopeng Chen, founder and CEO of Agile Robots. “Today, Agile Robots introduced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack, open reference humanoid built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, powered by Jetson Thor, giving developers a ready system to create, train and validate the capabilities needed to put humanoids to work.” Scheduled to be available in early 2027, Agile ONE SN is designed to advance frontier humanoid research and development, with interest from leading institutions such as Stanford University and ETH Zurich. New NVIDIA Technology Accelerate Robot Learning — From Data to Deployment New NVIDIA technologies help developers generate training data, scale robot learning, build simulation environments and deploy robot applications, reducing time to solution. SimReady Central Library offers more than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, while the Human 1M Dataset includes diverse human activities, synchronized three-view video and 3D hand tracking. Both are available on Hugging Face, with the full Human 1M Dataset accessible to Cosmos Coalition partners. NVIDIA Isaac Lab 3.0 is now generally available , providing an open source, agent-ready learning framework training and refining robot policies from desktop to data center using multi-GPU workflows and physics engines including Newton and NVIDIA PhysX ™. NVIDIA Isaac OS , an open source runtime framework built on NVIDIA Holoscan , connects AI, sensors, controls and robot hardware for deterministic, real-time performance from simulation to physical robots. NVIDIA is releasing three open source reference workflows for NVIDIA DGX Station ™ that help developers refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills in NVIDIA Isaac Lab and post-train NVIDIA Cosmos ™ world models for synthetic data generation using ChatGPT Astra. NVIDIA Halos provides a full-stack safety platform built on NVIDIA IGX Thor ™ to help move autonomous vehicles and robots from development to safer real-world deployment at scale.   SimReady Central Library on Hugging Face includes simulation-ready assets from Comau , FANUC, ForgeCAD, Franka Robotics, LG Electronics, Palatial, Robotiq, Standard Bots, Universal Robots and Vertiv. NVIDIA’s open source robot learning reference workflows running on DGX Station will be supported by solutions from 1X, Agile Robots, Humanoid, Maven Robotics, Mentee, MicroAGI, Rhoda, Sereact and Skild AI. Robotics partners are integrating NVIDIA Halos within their safety architectures, including Agile Robots, Agility, Dexory , FORT Robotics and KION for warehouse robot safety. SICK is evaluating Halos to advance dynamic safety for industrial robots, helping them respond to changing conditions beyond fixed zones. Advantech and NexCOBOT are developing NVIDIA IGX-based industrial computing platforms, while Reynolds & Moore, Accenture and TÜV SÜD are accelerating the certification process for the safe deployment of industrial physical AI. European Robotics Leaders Build on NVIDIA Open Technologies ABB Robotics is integrating NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries with RobotStudio HyperReality to simulate and virtually commission robotic systems before installation across a wide range of industries. KUKA Group is using Omniverse libraries in its Visual Components FactoryLens to add real-time rendering for factory simulation workflows. Sereact is using Isaac GR00T with Cosmos Transfer to train and post-train its Cortex platform for goods handling, running on Universal Robots industrial robot arms. events.title: ‘Jackdaw means we pay our mortgages’: relief in Aberdeen over gasfield approval
events.summary: Few believe decision will bring back city’s boom years, but workers hope it will secure North Sea jobs for now UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea What does the UK’s approval of Jackdaw mean? As recently as 2012, Aberdeen boasted the highest concentration of millionaires in the UK. An ATM reportedly had the highest withdrawal rate in Europe in the 90s, as oil and gas wealth flowed through the city. House prices soared in the scramble for space as fossil fuel firms transformed the city’s grand granite houses into company offices. But that was then. Today, “for sale” and “to let” signs punctuate the city’s main thoroughfares. Disposable income in Aberdeen has fallen by nearly 20% between 2013 and 2023 – more than any other large UK city – after a 2014 oil price shock sparked a brutal reversal in Aberdeen’s fortunes. At the beginning of this year, demolition began on the former offices of Marathon Oil, once a base for hundreds of workers. Between 2010 and 2021, the number of people aged 20-29 fell by 16%. BP appears set to leave the city after announcing plans to divest from its North Sea business. On darker days, the spectre of former coalmining towns looms large in the minds of some residents. “Years ago, a fund should have been set up that saved some of the oil money for Aberdeen . But that’s long gone,” said Scott, an assistant at a men’s clothing shop. “It’s a city centre like any other now. People blame the local council and the local government. I don’t know. It’s very different to how it was.” “Twenty years ago this street was full. Now it is so quiet,” said one woman at a bus stop on Union Street. For many Aberdonians, the government’s decision to approve the Jackdaw gasfield , located 150 miles offshore, came as a relief. Critics point to the climate impact and the modest number of jobs that the new gasfield would likely support. Tessa Khan, the executive director of the anti-oil campaign group Uplift, said: “Jackdaw will provide around just 2% of our gas demand for roughly 10 years. It has been oversold and won’t stop the overall decline in North Sea jobs as it will be largely unmanned and operated remotely.” The UN Environment Programme has said global carbon emission targets need to be cut by nearly a fifth in the next four years, and by close to half within a decade, to avoid overshooting climate targets by a disastrous margin. But for oil and gas workers in the city, this is about keeping as many North Sea jobs for as long as possible, which have so far not been replaced by the renewables sector and tend to pay less. At the heliport, offshore workers returning to dry land after a flight across stormy North Sea waters were in good spirits about the prospect of a new field. “Jackdaw means we pay our mortgages. Without oil and gas, what am I supposed to do?” said one woman, who works offshore as a cleaner on a rig. Another offshore worker said: “Short-term, the green industry isn’t going to replace this. It’s a slow process. You can’t expect it to happen overnight.” Few think that the new gasfield will restore the city’s boomtown years. Unlike other oil cities such as Houston, Abu Dhabi and Stavanger, Aberdeen has not been able to recover from the 2014 price shock and there is growing acceptance that the decline is permanent. Many offshore oil and gas workers acknowledge that they are likely to be the last generation of their kind – and increasingly work away for weeks at a time on rigs in Africa and Asia. More than 90% of the UK part of the North Sea basin has been exploited, compared with just over 50% in Norway, which has not outlawed new exploration licences. Jackdaw is projected to supply only 6% of the UK’s gas output at its peak. In the approval, the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, pointed to national security reasons behind her decision to back the project. “This decision will support the country’s energy security with homegrown gas this winter and help minimise the UK’s use of imported higher emission fuels as we continue our transition to renewables and nuclear. “The decision is compatible with our legally binding climate commitments, and we remain resolute in ending new licences for oil and gas and achieving net zero by 2050,” she said. The rapidly growing renewables industry in the city has proved to be a boon for some firms: the shipping operator North Star once made all of its money from the oil and gas sector, but now nearly 80% of its operating profit comes from offshore wind. Great British Energy is headquartered in the city. Yet, the growth in the offshore wind industry has so far failed to offset the decline in oil and gas jobs in Aberdeen, and it is unclear it ever will. About 90% of offshore jobs in the northeast of Scotland remain in the oil and gas sector, supporting around 38,000 jobs compare to 4,200 in the renewables sector. From the doldrums of the 2014 crash, Aberdeen has seen recent signs of recovery.

events.title: Inflation and government borrowing highest for a year ahead of next week's Budget
events.summary: Published 21 October 2026, 07:08 BST UK inflation and government borrowing both hit their highest in a year on Wednesday, adding to the pressure on Chancellor John Healey ahead of his first Budget in a week. The pace of UK price rises accelerated to 3.5% in the year to September, pushed up by sharp increases in petrol and diesel prices. The inflation figures came as UK government borrowing jumped to nearly £25bn in September, which means borrowing for the financial year to date is running £6bn above official forecasts. Healey has promised a Budget which will keep to Labour's commitment not to hike the three main taxes - income tax, National Insurance and VAT - while sticking to the party's fiscal rules. Inflation, the rate at which prices are rising, jumped from 3.1% in the year to August to 3.5% in the year to September. It is the highest inflation has been since October 2025, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). The cost of filling up a vehicle has soared in recent months as conflicts in the Middle East and Europe continue to squeeze global oil supplies. The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran after US and Israeli attacks has severely disrupted a major global supply line for crude oil, while oil refining capacity has been hampered globally by Russian and Ukrainian attacks on each other's infrastructure after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Petrol prices in September were the highest since August 2022, the ONS said, while diesel also rocketed. The average price of petrol rose by 8.2p per litre to 169.5p per litre between August and September, while diesel rose to 192.5p per litre. Motor fuel prices overall rose by 29.8% in the period covered by the figures. ONS chief economist Grant Fitzner said September's "notable" increase meant inflation was at its highest rate in almost a year. As well as fuel prices, the increase was driven by rising prices for airfares, computer games and live events, Fitzner said. September's inflation figure is also important because it suggests how benefits will increase next April. It means the state pension will most likely rise by 3.9%, in line with average wage rises from May to July, due to the triple lock. The inflation figure for September also dictates how other benefits will rise in April. By law, benefits such as personal independence payment (PIP) and carer's allowance must rise in line with September's consumer price index (CPI) measure of inflation. With a week to go until he delivers the Budget, Healey said: "We know that price rises from conflicts in the Middle East and Europe are hitting Britain and countries worldwide." He said the International Monetary Fund last week had praised the UK government for its "fiscal discipline", and that the government has just given the go-ahead for getting more gas from the North Sea's Jackdaw field . The Budget on 28 October will "keep up this momentum", he said, by sticking to the government's self-imposed fiscal rules, and by driving "growth in every postcode, while giving businesses and families some breathing space". But the inflation figure came as the ONS said the government borrowed £24.5bn in September, £1.8bn higher than a year earlier, as higher inflation helped to push up debt interest costs. The overshoot means, cumulatively, the government has borrowed £6bn more this year than the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), which scores government spending plans, had forecast. Despite overall debt topping £3tn for the first time, debt as a proportion of the UK's economic output - the measure used by the government to judge whether it is in line with its fiscal rules - fell. Faisal Islam: Inflation and borrowing figures illustrate chancellor's Budget challenge Published 9 hours ago The Conservatives said higher inflation and borrowing showed Labour had "lost control of the economy". Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith called for Healey to use his Budget to "tackle the deficit, and reduce the red tape and net zero costs that are driving up the cost of living for families". He added that the Conservatives would cut taxes, the costs of benefits and "wasteful" spending to "make our country prosperous again". Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the borrowing figures "painted a dismal picture" ahead of Healey's Budget. She said the amount borrowed in September was higher than analyst expectations as well as spending watchdog the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR)'s forecast. "This reinforces our view that the Chancellor will deliver a cautious Budget on 28 October that has little net impact on the economy and leaves the toughest fiscal choices for next year," she said.
