events.title: Inflation and government borrowing highest for a year ahead of next week's Budget
events.summary: Published 21 October 2026, 07:08 BST UK inflation and government borrowing both hit their highest in a year on Wednesday, adding to the pressure on Chancellor John Healey ahead of his first Budget in a week. The pace of UK price rises accelerated to 3.5% in the year to September, pushed up by sharp increases in petrol and diesel prices. The inflation figures came as UK government borrowing jumped to nearly £25bn in September, which means borrowing for the financial year to date is running £6bn above official forecasts. Healey has promised a Budget which will keep to Labour's commitment not to hike the three main taxes - income tax, National Insurance and VAT - while sticking to the party's fiscal rules. Inflation, the rate at which prices are rising, jumped from 3.1% in the year to August to 3.5% in the year to September. It is the highest inflation has been since October 2025, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). The cost of filling up a vehicle has soared in recent months as conflicts in the Middle East and Europe continue to squeeze global oil supplies. The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran after US and Israeli attacks has severely disrupted a major global supply line for crude oil, while oil refining capacity has been hampered globally by Russian and Ukrainian attacks on each other's infrastructure after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Petrol prices in September were the highest since August 2022, the ONS said, while diesel also rocketed. The average price of petrol rose by 8.2p per litre to 169.5p per litre between August and September, while diesel rose to 192.5p per litre. Motor fuel prices overall rose by 29.8% in the period covered by the figures. ONS chief economist Grant Fitzner said September's "notable" increase meant inflation was at its highest rate in almost a year. As well as fuel prices, the increase was driven by rising prices for airfares, computer games and live events, Fitzner said. September's inflation figure is also important because it suggests how benefits will increase next April. It means the state pension will most likely rise by 3.9%, in line with average wage rises from May to July, due to the triple lock. The inflation figure for September also dictates how other benefits will rise in April. By law, benefits such as personal independence payment (PIP) and carer's allowance must rise in line with September's consumer price index (CPI) measure of inflation. With a week to go until he delivers the Budget, Healey said: "We know that price rises from conflicts in the Middle East and Europe are hitting Britain and countries worldwide." He said the International Monetary Fund last week had praised the UK government for its "fiscal discipline", and that the government has just given the go-ahead for getting more gas from the North Sea's Jackdaw field . The Budget on 28 October will "keep up this momentum", he said, by sticking to the government's self-imposed fiscal rules, and by driving "growth in every postcode, while giving businesses and families some breathing space". But the inflation figure came as the ONS said the government borrowed £24.5bn in September, £1.8bn higher than a year earlier, as higher inflation helped to push up debt interest costs. The overshoot means, cumulatively, the government has borrowed £6bn more this year than the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), which scores government spending plans, had forecast. Despite overall debt topping £3tn for the first time, debt as a proportion of the UK's economic output - the measure used by the government to judge whether it is in line with its fiscal rules - fell. Faisal Islam: Inflation and borrowing figures illustrate chancellor's Budget challenge Published 9 hours ago The Conservatives said higher inflation and borrowing showed Labour had "lost control of the economy". Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith called for Healey to use his Budget to "tackle the deficit, and reduce the red tape and net zero costs that are driving up the cost of living for families". He added that the Conservatives would cut taxes, the costs of benefits and "wasteful" spending to "make our country prosperous again". Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the borrowing figures "painted a dismal picture" ahead of Healey's Budget. She said the amount borrowed in September was higher than analyst expectations as well as spending watchdog the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR)'s forecast. "This reinforces our view that the Chancellor will deliver a cautious Budget on 28 October that has little net impact on the economy and leaves the toughest fiscal choices for next year," she said. events.title: European Mobility Leaders Build Safe Vehicles and Robotaxi Fleets on NVIDIA Hyperion
events.summary: News Summary: Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets, with Volvo Cars adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for safe automated driving. NVIDIA introduces Halos SAFE, a new framework within the NVIDIA Halos safety system, which combines simulation and physical testing to help developers generate measurable, traceable AV safety evidence. NVIDIA announces Alpamayo 2 Edge, Alpamayo Agentic Factory and new Cosmos 3 Nano model variants to help developers build, customize and evaluate autonomous-driving for diverse vehicles, operating conditions and regions. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced that leading automakers in Europe and mobility providers, including Bolt with Lucid , Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride, are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets. In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale. Autonomous transportation represents a multitrillion-dollar opportunity, with robotaxis leading the move to commercial level 4 deployment. NVIDIA Hyperion and the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system give automakers and mobility providers the computing performance, safety foundation and long-term support to bring AVs and robotaxi fleets to market at scale. “Robotaxis are the first mass-market application of robotics and physical AI, reinventing how people and goods move,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “NVIDIA Hyperion, together with our Halos safety operating system, gives our partners a full-stack robotaxi platform designed to achieve full autonomy and the highest levels of safety, bringing us closer to a future where everything that moves is autonomous.” Mobility Leaders in Europe Build on NVIDIA Hyperion Automakers and mobility providers in Europe are pursuing various paths to autonomy, from passenger vehicles and robotaxi fleets to autonomous freight trucks. NVIDIA Hyperion’s modular architecture supports all of these programs, compatible with NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack autonomous driving software as well as partners’ own driving software. Bolt has selected NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for its European robotaxi program, beginning with future Lucid vehicles built on Hyperion. Bolt and NVIDIA will adapt the software for European roads and integrate it into vehicles from multiple manufacturers, combining NVIDIA’s driving and safety technologies with Bolt’s fleet-management systems, operations and local market expertise. Bolt plans to begin gathering real-world driving data to support the development and validation of the autonomous driving technology — subject to regulatory approval — in Madrid in 2027, with Germany being a priority for future deployment as part of a planned European rollout of at least 25,000 level 4-capable future Lucid vehicles built on NVIDIA Hyperion. At GTC Berlin, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles is presenting its autonomous ID. Buzz AD vehicle platform with Hyperion to support multiple autonomous-driving systems. Hyperion provides a common computing and sensor architecture designed to simplify integration and validation, helping developers and mobility operators bring robotaxi and commercial transport services to market. Volvo Cars is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with Hyperion, Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. Mercedes-Benz is extending its partnership with NVIDIA on Hyperion and Alpamayo Stack to support the development of the automaker’s L3 and L4 capabilities. The company also announced that MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO, developed in partnership with NVIDIA, will soon get approval for urban point-to-point urban driver assistance in Germany, helping drivers navigate journeys through complex city traffic. Beyond passenger vehicles and robotaxis, Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using Halos, Alpamayo and NVIDIA Cosmos ™ open world models to develop and validate its driving system, while TIER IV and the Technical University of Munich plan to integrate Hyperion to develop and validate systems for autonomous public transportation in Germany. NVIDIA technology and manufacturing partners are also helping expand the AV ecosystem, with Aptiv , Valeo and Schaeffler building Hyperion-based computing platforms that can be integrated by vehicle manufacturers for L4 AVs and robotaxis. Scaling Safe Autonomy With NVIDIA Halos Halos provides the safety foundation for NVIDIA’s AV platform, bringing together AI computing, safety software and validation from development through deployment. To give developers repeatable ways to evaluate driving behavior and simulation accuracy, NVIDIA today introduced Halos SAFE — the Safety Assurance Framework for Evaluation — with dSPACE, IVEX and TÜV Rheinland collaborating on evaluation workflows. Halos SAFE connects simulation, software- and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation, on-road testing and fleet monitoring through defined scenarios, tests and measurable performance criteria to generate traceable safety evidence that supports deployment. The Halos SAFE ecosystem also includes JLR, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo Cars, 51Sim, aiMotive , AVL, Deepen AI , Foretellix and Synopsys. Accelerating AV Development Developing AVs means teaching AI to handle the diversity of real-world driving, then bringing that intelligence into the vehicle. NVIDIA’s latest models, tools and blueprints help developers prepare driving data, improve models and evaluate performance: Alpamayo 2 Edge , a 2-billion-parameter reasoning model built on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge’s NVIDIA Nemotron™-based foundation, is optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor™ platform and designed to run at 10Hz for in-vehicle scene understanding and motion planning. AlpaJudge , a human-calibrated evaluation and reward model, scores driving explanations to assess reasoning quality, filter weak annotations and reduce manual review of training data. Foundation4D labels multicamera video without lidar input, supporting perception-model training and NVIDIA Omniverse™ NuRec scene reconstruction. events.title: Healthcare and Life Sciences Leaders Build on NVIDIA to Advance Drug Discovery and Expand Patient Care
events.summary: News Summary: NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design debut RFD4-Proteina, a new open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities, unlocking new frontiers in biology. Siemens Healthineers is advancing the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy, using NVIDIA intelligence to increase access to life-saving cancer care with agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and robotic control. Automata, Benchling, Biolevate, Boltz, Danaher, Hologen and Therna Biosciences are using the NVIDIA BioNeMo open platform to develop scientific agents that connect drug design, autonomous laboratories and biological discovery, helping researchers move from hypothesis to experiments faster. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced collaborations with leading global healthcare and research organizations to advance protein design — including through a newly released open model, RFD4-Proteina — accelerate drug discovery and bring greater precision to cancer care. Life sciences researchers must search vast biological design spaces and aim to shorten the cycle between computational design and laboratory testing to discover new medicines. Cancer care teams face a different challenge: translating complex imaging and treatment data into precise plans for each patient. NVIDIA open models, accelerated computing and physical intelligence can help experts evaluate more possibilities faster, from designing new proteins to planning adaptive radiotherapy. “Agentic and physical AI are opening new possibilities across medicine, from designing proteins and powering autonomous laboratories to improving personalized cancer care,” said Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare at NVIDIA. “Together with healthcare and life science leaders, we’re accelerating scientific discovery and advancing more precise, accessible care around the world.” NVIDIA and the UW Institute for Protein Design Introduce RFD4-Proteina Proteins are molecular tools that perform many of life’s essential tasks, and designing new versions could open paths to new medicines, diagnostics and industrial applications. But finding a protein capable of performing a designed function requires searching an immense range of possible designs. NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design are debuting RFD4-Proteina, a new NVIDIA BioNeMo™ open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities. The model generates targeted protein designs, enabling scientists and agents to search and refine designs using molecular inputs, constraints and scoring objectives. Potential applications include designing proteins to interrupt disease processes or detect signs of disease in diagnostic tests. In testing reported in the research draft, RFD4-Proteina achieved higher computational design success rates and generation throughput than the evaluated baselines across four benchmark suites: protein binding, small-molecule binding, enzyme scaffolding and DNA binding. The model helps researchers explore and prioritize candidates for laboratory testing, where experiments establish how a design performs under tested conditions. “We are moving from an era of discovering the proteins nature has made to one in which we can design entirely new ones,” said David Baker, 2024 Nobel Laureate in chemistry and director of the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington. “RFD4-Proteina expands what scientists can create, from proteins that could advance drug discovery to enzymes that break down pesticides. Making the model open will allow researchers around the world to build on these capabilities and pursue solutions once beyond the reach.” RFD4-Proteina is available today through partners including Amazon Bio Discovery, Anthropic’s Claude Science, Benchling, Databricks, Google Cloud, Hugging Face, Nebius, OpenAI and Tamarind Bio, enabling researchers and developers to integrate the open protein design model into agent, cloud and scientific computing workflows. Siemens Healthineers Advances Cancer Care With NVIDIA Siemens Healthineers and NVIDIA are collaborating to develop the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy with agentic and robotic intelligence, combining imaging and oncology expertise with accelerated computing and simulation to simplify workflows and expand access to care. By 2050, approximately 35 million people worldwide are projected to be diagnosed with cancer each year. Care teams face growing pressure to deliver precise, personalized treatment while managing limited specialist capacity. Greater efficiency can help expand access to care while maintaining the precision needed to deliver prescribed doses to tumors and protect surrounding healthy tissue. Siemens Healthineers is working with NVIDIA to further develop adaptive radiotherapy through agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and real-time computing. NVIDIA Nemotron ™ open foundation models are being explored to power agentic co-planning, with the aim of helping oncologists evaluate and refine personalized treatment strategies. The models could then be combined with NVIDIA CUDA ® -accelerated dose calculation for rapid patient-specific simulation and the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to connect live sensor data with AI and simulation to support adaptive treatment. “Adaptive radiotherapy is built on a single principle: treatment should adapt to the patient, not the other way around,” said Arthur Kaindl, head of Varian, the Siemens Healthineers cancer-care business. “We’ve made important advances in precision and adaptation — most recently, with the launch of the Accela system. Our collaboration with NVIDIA builds on that progress, exploring how AI and real-time computing could give clinicians greater speed and insight to make informed decisions, adapt treatment with greater confidence and deliver personalized care to more patients.” Scientific Agents Advance Drug Discovery and Development Life sciences is one of the world’s most important scientific frontiers, with global scientific R&D reaching $3.8 trillion and annual pharmaceutical budgets approaching $300 billion. events.title: NVIDIA, Nokia and Leading Telecom Operators Turn Networks Into Distributed Intelligence Platforms
events.summary: News Summary: Leading global telecom operators are expanding NVIDIA-powered computing across their networks to deliver advanced services closer to people and businesses, improve wireless experience and automate network operations. T-Mobile completes the world’s first AI-RAN call on a commercial network, while BT, Deutsche Telekom and Elisa announce AI-RAN pilots on live networks using Nokia’s CUDA-accelerated anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer, and NVIDIA introduces new Aerial RAN Computer configurations for high-capacity sites. Nine EMEA telecom operators are building and expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure across centralized and distributed locations. Operators and software partners are adopting NVIDIA Nemotron open models to deliver agentic services and develop agents for autonomous network operations.   GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced that leading global telecom operators are turning their networks into distributed intelligence platforms, adding NVIDIA accelerated computing to centralized data centers, metro sites and cell sites so they can serve models and applications closer to the people, businesses and machines that use them. T-Mobile has completed the world’s first AI-RAN call on a live network in Bellevue, Washington, with NVIDIA and Nokia. Deutsche Telekom is advancing physical AI for industries, and Orange is introducing new voice intelligence services for enterprises and emergency responders. Elisa has completed Europe’s first field trial of AI-RAN, running voice, mobile data and vision AI together on a single accelerated computing platform over 5G, and BT is preparing live AI-RAN trials in the U.K. Nokia is bringing its anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) for trials at BT, Deutsche Telekom, Elisa and Orange. Nine operators across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure, while Nokia and Cisco are incorporating NVIDIA Nemotron ™ open models into the software operators use to run autonomous networks. “Telecom networks were built to carry the world’s conversations. Now, they will also carry the world’s intelligence,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Leading global operators are turning their land, power and connectivity into a distributed AI infrastructure — bringing intelligence closer to the industries, people and robots that use it. With Nokia, we’re extending accelerated computing into the radio network itself, creating the foundation for AI-native 5G.” Intelligence is built in five layers : land, power and shell, chips, infrastructure, models and applications. Telecom operators already own sovereign infrastructure at the first layer, with data centers, regional sites and cell sites that have power, fiber and spectrum. By adding NVIDIA accelerated computing, open models and applications on top, operators are building the full intelligence stack into their networks. At distributed sites, a common converged platform based on the AI-RAN architecture can serve open models, power robotics, voice and agentic applications, and run intelligent 5G software. Europe’s Leading Telcos Build Distributed Infrastructure Infrastructure sits at the foundation of telecom’s transition to distributed service platforms. Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its NVIDIA-powered Industrial AI Cloud, which hosts open models — including NVIDIA Nemotron and Soofi — and serves robotics companies such as Agile Robots. At distributed sites, Deutsche Telekom is piloting AI-RAN trials with Nokia and NVIDIA, and demonstrating NVIDIA ARC to run inference between the device and the network edge. A GTC Berlin demonstration with Agile Robots shows the approach: on-robot intelligence handles real-time perception and action, a model at the distributed edge supports fine-tuning and coordination across robots, and the central infrastructure provides capacity for larger training workloads. Orange is hosting open models, including NVIDIA Nemotron, as a managed service on top of its Live Intelligence trusted AI platform, enabling new advanced services for enterprises. At distributed sites, Orange is deploying NVIDIA ARC for voice intelligence applications using Nemotron Speech, demonstrating new services to help emergency and field services teams translate across multiple languages in real time with low latency and reliability. Elisa has deployed NVIDIA ARC at a distributed network location, running a voice intelligence application that serves as an enterprise assistant, and is using open models to build edge applications. EMEA telcos are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure: New infrastructure: CRA in the Czech Republic, etisalat in the United Arab Emirates, Silknet in Georgia and TIM in Italy. Expansions: Cassava in Africa, Deutsche Telekom in Germany, Fastweb + Vodafone in Italy, Kazakhtelecom in Central Asia and Orion Telecom in Serbia.   AI-RAN Brings Accelerated Computing Into the Radio Network AI-RAN extends accelerated computing into the radio access network (RAN), turning it into an intelligence workload that runs on the same platform as advanced services, so operators can get more out of their spectrum while serving demand from sites close to users. Globally, nearly 20 telecom operators have publicly announced AI-RAN collaborations using Nokia anyRAN software and NVIDIA ARC. T-Mobile recently marked the world’s first AI-RAN call on its commercial network in Bellevue, Washington, running on commercial ARC servers, Nokia’s NVIDIA CUDA-accelerated RAN software and massive multiple-input multiple-output radios, and connected to an existing 5G Standalone core and a commercial smartphone. BT is planning live AI-RAN trials in Birmingham, England, with Nokia and NVIDIA in 2027. Deutsche Telekom has validated Nokia and NVIDIA’s commercial AI-RAN platform in Bonn and Oulu labs, including AI-enhanced uplink channel estimation to improve uplink user throughput, with plans to move to field trials in 2027. Elisa simultaneously ran voice, mobile data and video analytics on the NVIDIA ARC platform, marking a European first in Elisa’s over-the-air field environment using 5G spectrum. The trial clears the way for distributed deployment and commercial AI-RAN services in 2027. Orange is testing Nokia 5G software on NVIDIA ARC, focusing on AI-RAN spectral efficiency improvements and support for edge services in live networks.   NVIDIA is introducing two ARC configurations — MGX 2U and MGX 4U — designed for dense, high-capacity intelligence and radio workloads, typically deployed at centralized RAN sites. Powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO™ 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs , the configurations will offer x86 and NVIDIA Vera CPU options. events.title: Dubai records strong sales for homes valued at over $10m as it attracts wealthy despite Iran war
events.summary: Dubai recorded 86 residential transactions valued at $10 million or more during the third quarter this year, down 17 per cent annually, as wealthy investors continued to invest in the emirate despite the Iran war. Among the deals, 13 were for homes valued at more than $25 million, property consultancy Knight Frank said in its latest report on Wednesday. Of the total, the 73 that were in the $10 million to $25 million bracket had a combined value of Dh3.93 billion ($1.07 billion), with the remaining 13 transactions generating Dh1.84 billion. The highest-value transactions accounted for about 15 per cent of sales for more than $10 million by number, but nearly 32 per cent of their total value. “Despite the exceptional geopolitical backdrop across the region, Dubai’s luxury homes market has continued to record high volumes of sales during Q3, albeit these are lower than this time last year,” said Faisal Durrani, partner and head of research, Mena at Knight Frank. Prices across the city’s 10 prime neighbourhoods have dipped for the first time since 2020, declining by 5 per cent between the second and third quarters, he said. In total, prime transaction volumes are 29.4 per cent lower than this time last year. “The biggest drag at the moment on overall market activity is the ongoing regional conflict . The somewhat ‘stop-start’ nature of the hostilities is predictably a confidence dampener,” Mr Durrani said. Wealth inflows Dubai and Abu Dhabi continue to attract wealthy individuals on the back of government initiatives that support economic growth, including favourable tax environments, business-friendly policies and significant infrastructure investment. Net wealth in the UAE is set to jump to $6 trillion by the end of this decade despite the short-term volatility caused by the Middle East conflict , a report this month by Boston Consulting Group found. In the five years to the end of 2030, net wealth in the Emirates is set to increase by more than $2.3 trillion, at an annual growth rate of 10.6 per cent, the report said. Dubai and Abu Dhabi have also been ranked among the top 10 destinations for next-generation wealth despite current war-related concerns, Savills said in a report this week. Dubai was ranked eighth and the capital 10th among favoured cities for the $84 trillion of wealth expected to be transferred between generations over the next two decades, it said. In the first nine months of the year, a total of 412 transactions worth $10 million or more were recorded in Dubai, up 15 per cent on an annual basis, Knight Frank's latest report found. The combined value of the deals this year stood at about $6.67 billion, the report said. On a quarterly basis, transaction volumes in the third quarter were down about 34 per cent from the previous period, the report said. Palm Jumeirah tops list In terms of areas of Dubai, Palm Jumeirah recorded the most residential sales worth $10 million or more in the third quarter, with 27 transactions worth Dh2.01 billion, Knight Frank found. The community accounted for approximately 31 per cent of luxury homes sold between July and September and 35 per cent of their total value. “The easing of prices by 9.1 per cent over the last 12-months means the island is increasingly offering ‘good value’ at Dh4,083 per square foot,” said Louis Harding, partner and head of UAE residential at Knight Frank. “Buyer interest here continues to largely stem from those seeking a permanent or holiday home, rather than buy-to-flip investors.” Jumeirah ranked second by transaction volume, followed by Emirates Hills, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Golf Estates.

events.title: NVIDIA Agent Toolkit Expands, Grounding Enterprise Agents in Company Data
events.summary: Agents are only as useful as what they know, and only as trustworthy as the boundaries they run within. Leading enterprises are using the open source NVIDIA Agent Toolkit — now expanded with new tools — to customize and control agents, use company data to inform their answers and actions, monitor what they do and govern how they operate. The new NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation with NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries NVIDIA open models including Nemotron Retriever and the new Kumo family NVIDIA OpenShell secure agent runtime NVIDIA NemoClaw secure agent blueprints Tools and skills, like NeMo Relay and NeMo Compass To develop agents that accomplish real work and are trustworthy from development to deployment, builders need an open agent stack that brings together the models, harness, runtime, data and tools. NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation helps enterprises turn data into company intelligence agents can use. Agents can find relevant information, understand what it means for the business and use it to make predictions and help people decide what to do next. Companies can use Agent Knowledge Foundation without moving data, rebuilding existing workflows or changing governance controls. The foundation features NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries , including cuDF, cuGraph, cuML, cuOpt and cuVS, and the new Auto-Ontology library, which translates raw company data into familiar business concepts — like customers, products and orders — and maps how they relate. It also includes NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever and Kumo Structured open models — Kumo Tabular, Kumo Relational, Kumo Time Series and Kumo Forecast — which help agents find relevant company information to answer questions and make predictions. OpenShell provides the secure runtime boundary, giving enterprises control over what agents can access and do. NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints provide reference designs for building secure, specialized agents. The newest NemoClaw blueprint for agent optimization provides a step-by-step starting point for improving agent intelligence — making them better at their jobs over time. Enterprises Adopt NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation The new NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation is already at work across enterprises. With Palantir , NVIDIA’s supply chain organization is using Agent Knowledge Foundation through Palantir Foundry, Ontology and AIP to deploy specialized agents, create actionable intelligence from proprietary data, predict outcomes and optimize decision-making. Databricks pairs NVIDIA Kumo Anomaly with Databricks Genie Ontology to power context-aware agents. Snowflake is enabling customers to use the NVIDIA Kumo Engine and Kumo Relational open models in their Snowflake Notebook environments to unlock more predictive capabilities. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models make search faster and more accurate. Using the embedding model, Amazon OpenSearch Service improved relevance with fewer search steps and virtually no added latency. SAP ’s fine-tuned reranker ran nearly 3x faster. ServiceNow improved reranking quality while cutting latency by nearly a quarter. Zoom is using Nemotron Retriever models to improve document understanding, search relevance and context retrieval for Zoom AI Services. Amazon Web Services (AWS) , ClickHouse , Cloudera , Cohesity , Dassault Systèmes , Dell , Elastic , Exa , IBM , NetApp , Oracle , Perplexity , Starburst and VAST Data are also among those building on Agent Knowledge Foundation. Learn more by joining this GTC Berlin session on building, deploying and optimizing specialized agents in production . events.title: NVIDIA Open Models Advance Europe’s Sovereign Intelligence Across Industries
events.summary: NVIDIA is expanding its family of open models across language, robotics, biology, and quantum computing, giving developers, researchers and enterprises what they need to build applications tailored to local languages and industries The portfolio includes the new NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models; new NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models for embedding, reranking and document parsing; the new NVIDIA Kumo family open weight foundation models and libraries for structured business data; NVIDIA Cosmos 3.5 world models; NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge for autonomous vehicles; NVIDIA BioNeMo for healthcare and scientific discovery; and NVIDIA Ising for quantum computing. The open models give organizations a foundation they can customize with local data and deploy on infrastructure they control. NVIDIA Nemotron Powers Post-Training Across Industries NVIDIA Nemotron brings open language models, datasets and recipes to developers building agents. The models support text and images, helping agents orchestrate workflows, reason through complex problems and complete specialized tasks at a lower cost. Nemotron models are built with data, research and expertise from the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition , including European partners Black Forest Labs , H-Company and Mistral . Nemotron provides a foundation for enterprises to build applications based on their own knowledge and expertise. Dassault Systèmes , Domyn , Dream , Palantir’s customers , Salesforce , SAP , Shopify , Synopsys and WPP , as well as professional services providers like Accenture and EY, are working with Nemotron models and datasets to create custom models and build domain-specific agents. A broad ecosystem of post-training partners, including AfterQuery , AgileRL , AI21 , Alice , Applied Compute , Baseten , CoreWeave , Distil Labs , EON , Fastino , Fireworks , Google Cloud, Mercor , Multiverse Computing , Nebius , Handshake AI , Plurai , Prime Intellect , River.AI, Scale AI , Trajectory and TNG, is helping enterprises customize Nemotron for domain-specific workloads. NVIDIA Kumo Speeds Agents’ Work With Structured Enterprise Data NVIDIA Kumo open foundation models, libraries and tools help agents and applications forecast outcomes, score fraud risk and recommend actions from structured business data. Part of NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation , Kumo shortens time to prediction and reduces the cost and complexity of building a separate machine learning pipeline for every task. Developers can use pretrained Kumo models to bring predictions to more applications quickly, then fine-tune them using proprietary data when higher performance is critical. The portfolio includes NVIDIA Kumo Structured , with models for relational and tabular prediction, forecasting and anomaly detection, and NVIDIA Kumo Engine , an open library stack for developing and deploying structured data foundation models. Cognite , Coinbase , Databricks , DoorDash , Revolut and Tubi are among the first to work with Kumo models to accelerate development. Snowflake customers are already using Kumo models to accelerate AI development in industries including advertising, energy, financial services and retail. NVIDIA Cosmos Accelerates Robotics Training and Simulation NVIDIA Cosmos is a family of open world foundation models that helps developers build robots, autonomous vehicles and vision agents that understand and interact with the physical world. NVIDIA is introducing new Cosmos post-training and optimization tools to help developers improve world models using less compute, along with simulation checkpoints for evaluating behavior in interactive driving and robotic manipulation scenarios before real-world testing. NVIDIA is also introducing Cosmos Data Factory — comprising blueprints and core agent skills — to help developers curate, label, generate and evaluate training data for driving scenarios, product defects, image augmentation and event generation. Developers can use complete workflows or individual capabilities with agents coordinating the process. Porsche with Voxel51 , ANYbotics with Encord , Zalando and CEVA Logistics with Sereact , and Siemens are using Cosmos Data Factory to create high-quality, diverse training datasets and improve model precision. NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Brings Real-Time Reasoning to Autonomous Vehicles NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is a compact reasoning model that brings real-time scene understanding and motion planning directly into autonomous vehicles. Built on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge’s Nemotron-based foundation and optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor platform, it helps developers bring advanced driving capabilities into vehicles with lower computing requirements. NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina Advances Protein Design NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina is an open protein design model from NVIDIA and the Baker Lab at the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design. The model generates protein sequences and 3D structures to help researchers design proteins that bind to difficult targets, assemble into complex structures and bind to small molecules. NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina delivers leading performance across more than 10 protein design tasks and generates designs about 13x faster than RFdiffusion3 in a benchmark of 200 amino acid proteins. Researchers can use the model through agents to generate and evaluate candidates against design goals and molecular constraints, then choose which designs to test in the lab. NVIDIA Ising Accelerates Quantum Development The NVIDIA Ising family of open models provides a common, extensible foundation to speed the breakthroughs needed to develop useful quantum supercomputers, from real-time hardware calibration to error correction, across different qubit modalities and tailored to individual hardware needs. IQM Quantum Computers is using Ising to calibrate its quantum processors, showcasing how specialized open calibration models outperform large general-purpose models. SEEQC is combining the NVIDIA NVQLink platform and Ising with its unique Digital Link to meet the low-latency requirements needed for real-time quantum error correction. AWS is making NVIDIA Ising readily available to researchers by integrating the model family into AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS). While decoding is typically performed on classical hardware colocated with the quantum processor due to latency requirements, the AWS PCS integration lets researchers build on Ising prior to deployment. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available on Hugging Face , ModelScope , OpenRouter and build.nvidia.com as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as through NVIDIA cloud, post-training and inference partners. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is expected to be available on Friday, Oct. 23. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever open models are available on Hugging Face , various partner platforms, and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice on build.nvidia.com .

events.title: “The River Can’t Be Trusted”
events.summary: Reese Drive, crossing the Rio Ruidoso in New Mexico, lies near where the body of a child, Sebastian Trotter, was found. He and his sister, Charlotte, were swept away by a July 2025 flood. Peak tourist season had arrived in Ruidoso, New Mexico, and Mayor Lynn Crawford was campaigning to convince the public that the village was safe. A Republican with white hair and a Texas drawl, Crawford said he was frustrated with residents who were sharing warnings of flooding on social media. “They spout stuff off,” he said in a radio address on June 30, 2025. “And I don’t know why they’re so afraid. I do not understand it.”  The community had experienced severe flooding the previous summer, after two wildfires burned 25,000 acres above town, in the Sacramento Mountains. The fires and floods had destroyed about 1,000 homes. Together, the Village of Ruidoso and its smaller neighbor, Ruidoso Downs, are home to some 10,000 residents, but that number more than doubles during the summer. Since then, residents had been on edge. A new monsoon season had arrived, bringing sporadic flooding that jeopardized the town’s economic engine of horse racing. At stake were big crowds to celebrate the Fourth of July, watch quarter horse racing and enjoy cool weather that’d lured Texans here for generations. “We have flooding temporarily,” Crawford had told a Texas news anchor in an interview. “And just almost as fast as it came to town, and went through town, it’s gone.” Crawford, who is 64, managed an exclusive club at the Ruidoso Downs Race Track & Casino and once called that his “real job.” He made less than $26,000 as mayor. But if the town’s economy was precarious, so was its geography. The South Fork and Salt fires charred the landscape, leaving soils that didn’t easily absorb water. Imagine spilling hot wax on a carpet, letting it cool and repeatedly pouring water over it. Now place the wax on steep hills above a river lined with log homes, tourist shops selling wooden bears and an iconic racetrack.  Officials were aware of the threat but clung to Ruidoso’s animating idea: that nature could be subdued for the enjoyment of tourists and profit of the community. Nowhere was this more apparent than at the track, where the Rio Ruidoso, channeled through culverts, crossed the infield. After the 2024 flooding damaged the track, the culverts had been rebuilt with a $16 million public investment authorized by New Mexico’s Democratic governor, Michelle Lujan Grisham. The track had only recently reopened, and flooding was again threatening to derail the racing season. On June 26, internal records show, Ruidoso’s emergency management department was at a heightened threat awareness level. Flooding had destroyed a bridge upstream of the town, and the forecast called for more rain.  But publicly, the village maintained it was prepared and the community was safe. The next day, the emergency manager reduced the threat level a notch, and the communications department chided residents for sharing warnings of catastrophic flooding on social media, noting that some posts featured old videos. “Protect our community from fear-based falsehoods,” the village implored in a public service announcement. Village of Ruidoso Mayor Lynn Crawford, shown in his office, was presiding at a council meeting when the flood hit. On July 4, and one state over, violent flooding killed more than 130 people in central Texas. But multiple tourists who were arriving in Ruidoso said they had no idea the town was in danger. At the racetrack, the horses ran, and Crawford hosted members at the Ruidoso Jockey Club, where private tables cost as much as six figures. That weekend, Sebastian Trotter and his family traveled to Ruidoso from El Paso, Texas. Trotter was an Army helicopter pilot stationed at Fort Bliss; his wife, Stephanie, was a nursing student. They thought the place looked family friendly; they saw no warnings online. They brought their two children and three dogs. On Sunday, July 6, they parked their trailer in a desirable spot on the water’s edge at the Riverview RV Park. In online photos, the river appeared gentle. “You could go put your toes in,” said Sebastian. That day, the Rio Ruidoso — “noisy river,” in Spanish — briefly flooded and firefighters rescued at least four people. The Trotters saw the water rise, but the campground host said it was a regular occurrence. Then the river receded. In the park, the Trotters’ children, Sebastian Rowan, 7, and Charlotte, 4, biked under the tall pines. The boy was a soccer player who was enchanted by the idea of camping in the woods; Charlotte was bright and cheery, sometimes applying glitter to her father’s mustache. Later, the family walked through the village, where elk and wild horses occasionally graze near tourists. On Tuesday, July 8, the Trotters were visiting a lake when they saw clouds form. They decided to head into town, ordering pizza before allowing the children to pick out souvenirs. The younger Sebastian selected a rainbow gemstone, Charlotte a bracelet and a ring. Then they returned to the RV park, where they relaxed by the river.  At 1 p.m., Crawford presided over a council meeting at Village Hall. He began by recognizing the Texas flood victims and nodding to Ruidoso’s relative success. “We want to keep all of central Texas in our thoughts and prayers and see how bad it was and how fortunate we’ve been,” he said. “The goal of the village is to protect the village.” That meant balancing public safety with tourism, he said. Read More Town Leaders Said They Were Prepared for Floods. First Responders Disagree. At almost the same moment, storm clouds gathered in the mountains. Even short periods of moderate rain on severe burn scars can unleash post-fire floods. By 1:30 p.m., radar indicated storms might douse both scars simultaneously. A little before 2 p.m., firefighters texted images of the radar to one another. “It could be interesting,” wrote one. Only about a third of the department was on duty at the time and the chief, Cade Hall, had for weeks declined to preposition additional flood specialists near low-lying areas. Hall disputed ProPublica’s reporting about the emergency response but declined to comment with specifics. Less than an hour later, another flood arrived, carrying debris that backed up behind bridges. The water kept coming, fanning onto roads until the normal course of the river disappeared. What the wall of brown water carried told residents it was time to panic. Jason Fulcher, an owner of the Riverview RV Park, saw a tree-size log in the waterway. Two miles downstream, a maintenance worker at a mobile home park saw a car float past and lodge against a bridge. Farther downstream, the track’s executives did not need physical signs of danger; they knew what was coming because they’d been alerted. But the Trotters were caught unprepared. events.title: Town Leaders Said They Were Prepared for Floods. First Responders Disagree.
events.summary: A Ruidoso Fire Department station less than a half mile from the Riverview RV Park. The fire chief had for weeks declined requests from off-duty swiftwater technicians who wanted to be stationed in flood-prone areas, including one close to the RV park, before the waters hit. The man was nearly to his waist in a flooded river and couldn’t get out. A firefighter and a police officer didn’t have enough rope or manpower to lift him onto the temporary flood barrier that separated them from the debris-strewn water. The man, Jere Stark, had just been carried a quarter mile by a torrential flood and was covered in mud and extremely cold. It was around 3:30 p.m. on July 8, 2025, and a flood in Ruidoso, New Mexico, had unleashed chaos at Paradise Canyon Drive, just a couple hundred yards from the headquarters of the village fire department. Not far from Stark, a woman huddled on the ground, shielded from the floodwaters by the temporary barrier. It was Stephanie Trotter, a tourist from El Paso, Texas, who had been washed away with her young daughter. A civilian tended to her while a second firefighter hauled in a rope he had used to rescue her. “Is somebody coming for her?” asked the civilian. By that time, at least eight other firefighters were trying to save people upstream at the Riverview RV Park, where Trotter and Stark had been staying. But at the barrier where Stark was waiting for help, the two firefighters and one police officer were the only first responders. One of the firefighters wasn’t even wearing a personal flotation device — a basic safety measure for flood rescues. They soon got help from civilians, including a property owner in shorts and flip-flops and a second passerby who both helped one of the firefighters haul Stark from the water with another rope. Body-camera footage from a Ruidoso Police Department officer shows the moment that a civilian, Corey Sexton, and others pulled Jere Stark from the flood. Obtained by ProPublica Trotter and two civilians told the police officer, Jimmy Hernandez, that her family was missing. Lost in the flood were her 4-year-old daughter, her 7-year-old son and her husband.  Hearing this, Hernandez radioed, “We need swiftwater rescue here.” But no additional swiftwater teams arrived for at least 25 minutes. Both children died, along with an adult man. Trotter’s husband, Sebastian, survived. The shortage of firefighters at Paradise Canyon Drive illustrates larger problems with Ruidoso’s emergency response that day. Five rescuers involved in the effort said the village’s leadership had not given them enough training or dispatched enough of them in advance of the flooding to protect the community. Because of the flood’s strength, rescuers said, the best chance to save the Trotters’ children was before the water arrived, when they could have evacuated the area where the family was camping. But they said the fire chief, Cade Hall, had for weeks resisted calls to station additional flood experts in low-lying areas when there was a threat of storms. Doing so would have required paying firefighters overtime. “The village’s mentality is, ‘We’ll have to pay for that, and what if nothing happens?’” said one rescuer in an interview earlier this year. ProPublica reported that village leaders knew dangerous floods were likely because two intense 2024 wildfires had scarred the hillsides above town. Even moderate rain on severe burn scars can trigger post-fire floods and debris flows. But leaders seeking to encourage tourism scolded residents who warned of the danger on social media. We also examined what went wrong with the rescue itself, consulting with seven experts outside Ruidoso who have experience in emergency response including floods. The Village of Ruidoso did not respond to detailed written questions about its emergency response, and it has not publicly released a report on rescue efforts during the flood. Reached by phone, Hall disputed ProPublica’s reporting but declined to provide specifics. Mayor Lynn Crawford has said protecting the village includes balancing public safety with tourism, the lifeblood of its economy. Read More “The River Can’t Be Trusted” The fire department employed nine swiftwater technicians trained to perform rescues in floodwater. But when forecasters issued a flash flood warning due to heavy rain, only a handful were working, along with four New Mexico National Guard technicians in vehicles capable of navigating floods. According to a spokesperson for the Guard, its members helped rescue nine people from the flood. Two additional swiftwater teams had recently been in Ruidoso. But when the weather forecast for the area showed a slightly decreased chance of flash flooding in late June, the state’s Department of Homeland Security and Emergency Management issued an order to send home the team from Las Cruces. One member of that team, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to protect their employment, said, “We didn’t understand why we were being sent home.” The other swiftwater team, which was from Texas, left after deadly flooding hit Kerr County and surrounding regions in its home state.  A former incident commander for Cal Fire, California’s fire agency, said that the state shared responsibility for the inadequate emergency response on July 8 because of its decision to send home the Las Cruces team. “This should be a clarion call as to reevaluating their resource availability.” Asked about the decision, a DHSEM spokesperson said in an email, “New Mexico was experiencing multiple flooding threats,” adding that the team needed to be available to respond elsewhere. According to the spokesperson, there are only about eight swiftwater teams in the state. But the Las Cruces team was not deployed to another flood. Rather, it went home. “I could understand if we were sent somewhere else,” said the frustrated swiftwater technician. This left Ruidoso’s firefighters to lead rescue operations in the village. But Hall had for weeks declined requests from off-duty swiftwater technicians who wanted to be stationed in flood-prone areas before the waters hit. One of those areas was close to the Riverview RV Park, where Stark and the Trotter family were staying. Stephanie and Sebastian Trotter’s trailer was destroyed during the flooding at the Riverview RV Park. Forty-five minutes before the downpour started, Crawford had stated in a council meeting that whenever the village was alerted to flooding, firefighters and public works employees would be at the ready: “Everybody is in position.”  Over the coming two hours, these words would prove false.  At 2:12 p.m. the National Weather Service sent out a flash flood warning. About 20 minutes later, Hall summoned all off-duty swiftwater technicians. events.title: Parents and teachers in England: share your views on two-week half terms
events.summary: We would like to hear from parents and teachers about their thoughts and experiences of two-week half terms While it used to be standard for state schools in England to have one-week half terms, some pupils and staff are being given a fortnight off. Councils set the holiday dates for state schools in England, while academies, free schools, foundation schools and voluntary-aided schools can set their own. Most schools still opt for one week, but more around the country are moving to, or considering the move to, a two-week break. In the past, parents with young children have the said the longer holiday places an extra burden on them to find childcare . In Wales, plans to extend the half-term and reduce the summer term were shelved in 2024 after opposition from the teaching unions. We would like to hear from parents and teachers about their thoughts and experiences of two-week half terms. Do you think they are a good idea or not? Do you have a fortnight off? Do you have any concerns? You can share your response using this form. Please include as much detail as possible. Please note, the maximum file size is 5.7 MB . Your contact details are helpful so we can contact you for more information. They will only be seen by the Guardian. If you include other people's names please ask them first. events.title: Non-Iran Middle East oil exports recover to prewar levels with Hormuz alternatives
events.summary: Non-Iran Middle East oil exports have surpassed prewar levels as ships continued to transit through the Strait of Hormuz , a key route for global oil supplies, despite rise in attacks on vessels. The total oil flows, including shipments through Hormuz and alternative routes across the region, averaged more than 24.5 million barrels per day for the week ended October 18, surpassing the 24.4 million bpd for the week ending February 22, just before the Iran war broke out, according to preliminary data from Kpler. The total volumes recorded include Hormuz transits, Gulf of Oman ship to ship net exports, Gulf of Oman terminal loadings from Fujairah and Oman ports and Red Sea exports. The data excludes Iranian exports. The data is an estimate which is subject to change depending on ship crossings across the strait at a given time. The conflict began on February 28 with the US and Israel attacking Iran. Tehran retaliated with attack s on its Gulf neighbours and ships carrying oil through the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow water channel in the Arabian Gulf. The strait has been subject to an Iranian blockade since the start of the conflict, but ships are continuing to transit make it through, with about 19 commodity vessels crossing on a daily basis in the last 10 days, the data shows. More than 100 ships a day used to cross the strait before the war, carrying oil, fertilisers and refined products to global markets. But Iranian attacks have resulted in ship owners avoiding the channel. According to International Maritime Organisation data, there have been 116 attacks on ships up to October 20, with 24 deaths since the conflict began. Attacks have increased recently. The US also plans to allow ships that are under sanctions to sail through the channel that is expected to help increase flows to global markets. The dark fleet, sometimes referred to as the shadow fleet, refers to a group of ships that sail outside conventional shipping regulations. These vessels use deceptive shipping practices to transport cargo that is under sanctions or at high risk, deliberately concealing it to avoid detection. The US administration's plan would involve investors buying and refurbishing the idle vessels before using them to transport legitimate oil. Oil continues to trade higher amid the Middle East conflict, with Brent, the benchmark for two thirds of the world's oil, trading above $110 a barrel at 1.16pm UAE time on Wednesday. West Texas Intermediate, the gauge that tracks US crude, was nearing $100 per barrel.

events.title: NVIDIA Launches OpenShell Reference Architecture for Safe AI Agents
events.summary: News Summary: The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture delivers enterprise governance, isolation and security for building, containing, observing and enforcing safe agents across enterprise infrastructure and edge systems. Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture brings together NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. The OpenShell Reference Architecture extends to the edge with NVIDIA RTX Spark, NVIDIA DGX Spark and NVIDIA DGX Station systems. The OpenShell Reference Architecture runs on leading enterprise operating systems, including Canonical, Red Hat, and Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Execution Containers. Anthropic, AWS, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Dassault Systèmes, Dell Technologies, Google Cloud, HPE, IBM, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Perplexity, SAP, ServiceNow, Siemens, SpaceX Super Intelligence and others are among those working with the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enhance the security of agent deployments. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture , which enables building, containing, observing and enforcing safe agents on enterprise infrastructure and edge systems. The OpenShell Reference Architecture builds on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell ™ secure runtime software, extending it into full-stack, industrial-scale infrastructure for agent development and operations. It includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for running enterprise workloads, including closed and open models built with NVIDIA Nemotron ™; NVIDIA Vera CPUs for operating agent harnesses; open source NVIDIA OpenShell software; and NVIDIA BlueField ® DPUs for running the NVIDIA Sentry unified security software framework that provides continuous out-of-band monitoring of agent behavior and in-silicon policy enforcement. The OpenShell Reference Architecture is extensible to agents running at the edge across industries such as retail, healthcare, manufacturing, robotics, software development and telecommunications with NVIDIA RTX Spark ™, NVIDIA DGX Spark ™ and NVIDIA DGX Station ™ systems. “AI capability and safety must advance together,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “As enterprises prepare to deploy billions of AI agents, safety and control must be built into the computing architecture. NVIDIA created OpenShell to give agents the freedom to do useful work within clearly defined boundaries — contained, monitored and under control. With the OpenShell Reference Architecture, agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera and be governed on BlueField.” Full-Stack Infrastructure Built for Agents The OpenShell Reference Architecture features NVIDIA accelerated computing paired with software for secure agent operations. NVIDIA Vera Rubin , with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 infrastructure at its core, is fungible across pretraining, post-training and inference. For agentic workloads, NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems deliver 30x higher throughput per megawatt. NVIDIA Vera CPUs deliver 2x the performance of x86 processors with greater energy efficiency and run NVIDIA OpenShell , which provides a secure runtime boundary for autonomous agents. NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs continuously monitor agent behavior with NVIDIA Sentry , built on NVIDIA DOCA ™ software. BlueField and NVIDIA Sentry together provide in-silicon security enforcement — if an agent attempts to move outside its software boundary, NVIDIA Sentry quarantines and stops it in milliseconds. NVIDIA Sentry, powered by DOCA and running on BlueField-4, boosts agent capacity by up to 20%. NVIDIA Partners Building Secure Agent Deployments With OpenShell NVIDIA is working with industry leaders building infrastructure, models and software to enable industries to safely deploy agents in production. The OpenShell Reference Architecture runs on leading enterprise operating systems and container orchestration layers, including Linux and Kubernetes infrastructure powered by Canonical, SUSE and Red Hat , as well as Microsoft Windows using Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC). It can run on cloud operating systems from Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. Enterprises can run agents from model builders including Anthropic, Cohere, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Perplexity, Reflection and SpaceX Super Intelligence on OpenShell infrastructure. NVIDIA is also working with model builder partners on OpenShell deployments for advanced model research. Cybersecurity leaders 1Password, Check Point , CrowdStrike , Cisco , F5 , Fortinet, Microsoft, Okta, Palo Alto Networks , TrendAI and Zscaler are integrating support for the OpenShell Reference Architecture into their agent security solutions. Leading banks — including Europe’s BBVA and Santander — are working with NVIDIA to explore the OpenShell Reference Architecture as a framework for strengthening agent safety, security and governance. Enterprise software leaders Cadence , Dassault Systèmes , IBM, SAP , Siemens and Synopsys are working with OpenShell to build agent software platforms. Palantir and NVIDIA are working with customers to deploy secure agents in production. SAP is integrating the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture with Joule Studio runtime, part of SAP Business AI Platform, connecting business governance with secure agent execution. ServiceNow today announced the general availability of ServiceNow Arc, a personal long-running AI agent with actions governed at runtime by the ServiceNow Super Intelligence Control Tower and enforced by NVIDIA OpenShell. In addition, ServiceNow’s recently announced AI Passport authority layer carries those policies to NVIDIA OpenShell and NVIDIA Sentry, so enterprises can revoke an AI agent’s access across software and hardware within seconds. NVIDIA system manufacturers Dell Technologies , Cisco , HPE , Lenovo and Supermicro are among those building infrastructure with the OpenShell Reference Architecture. NVIDIA is also working with cloud service providers including CoreWeave, Crusoe, Firebird, Firmus, GMI Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Vultr to deploy OpenShell-ready infrastructure. Inference and post-training service providers including Baseten, Deepinfra, Fireworks and Together AI are building OpenShell Reference Architecture integrations into their model development pipelines. events.title: European Ecosystem Builds World’s Most Efficient AI Factories With NVIDIA DSX
events.summary: News Summary:  NVIDIA DSX reference designs use closed-loop liquid cooling and dry coolers to enable near-zero facility cooling water consumption, with potential savings of 54 million liters a day for a 2-gigawatt deployment — equivalent to the daily water use of 180,000 households. AI clouds in Europe are building and operating NVIDIA DSX-based AI factories, expanding access to accelerated computing for the continent’s enterprises, developers and governments. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS software helps operators use up to 30% less power to generate the same number of tokens, with CoreWeave, Firmus, Google Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale and Sharon AI planning to use the technology, while DSX Flex software turns AI factories into flexible power loads to support grid reliability and enable faster grid connection. NVIDIA SimReady Central, a hub for simulation-ready digital models of physical equipment, launches on Hugging Face with validated power and cooling assets, helping operators build and simulate DSX AI factory digital twins faster. New NVIDIA DSX OS open source software automates infrastructure lifecycle and improves health automation as well as resiliency capabilities to help operators run AI factories at scale. An expanding ecosystem — including technology and industrial AI leaders AVEVA, Dassault Systèmes and Siemens, and energy and cooling providers ABB, Eaton, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, Schneider Electric, Siemens Energy, Trane Technologies and Vertiv — is connecting AI factory design, power, cooling and operations to support Europe’s accelerated computing buildout.   GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced that Europe’s leading ecosystem partners are adopting the NVIDIA DSX™ AI Factory Platform to build AI factories that minimize water consumption for cooling and use less power for the same AI output. The platform also helps partners bring new capacity online faster and adapt workload power consumption to support grid reliability.   NVIDIA DSX is a full-stack AI factory reference architecture, co-innovated with the world’s leading infrastructure companies. Compute, networking, storage, software, power and cooling are codesigned as one system — optimized from design to operation.  AI clouds and leading design, construction, energy and cooling providers are using DSX to build and operate infrastructure serving Europe’s enterprises, developers and governments. “Europe’s technology leadership depends on how efficiently we turn power and infrastructure into intelligence,” said Warren Barkley, vice president of DSX product management at NVIDIA. “NVIDIA DSX brings together the technologies and ecosystem expertise operators need to build responsibly, operate efficiently at scale and bring intelligence to the market faster.” The NVIDIA DSX platform includes DSX MaxLPS™ for dynamic power allocation, DSX Flex for coordinating workload power consumption with grid conditions, DSX Reference Design for validated infrastructure architectures, DSX Sim™ for simulation, DSX OS™ for infrastructure management and DSX Exchange™ for connecting computing and facility systems. These technologies help operators design, deploy and run AI factories that save valuable resources.  NVIDIA DSX Rethinks Cooling Conventional cooling towers remove heat by evaporating water, requiring a continual supply of replacement water. NVIDIA DSX reference designs connect liquid-cooled computing with dry-cooler-based heat rejection that avoids evaporation: Cooling liquid absorbs heat from computing equipment and circulates in a closed loop, while outdoor dry coolers, similar to large radiators, release that heat into the air without evaporating water. NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure supports 100% liquid cooling with coolant temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius. With dry-cooler-based designs, this architecture can reduce facility cooling water consumption to near zero. At 2-gigawatt scale, NVIDIA DSX can save 54 million liters of water a day compared with conventional cooling-tower-based systems — equivalent to the daily water use of 180,000 households. Local climate determines whether supplemental mechanical cooling is needed during the hottest periods. Delivering the Same AI Output With Less Power Power availability defines how much capacity operators can bring online. DSX MaxLPS and DSX Flex address this constraint. DSX MaxLPS dynamically allocates power within an AI factory’s provisioned budget, helping operators generate the same number of tokens with up to 30% less power. Operators can also use this efficiency to support more GPU capacity and higher throughput within existing power budgets. CoreWeave, Firmus, Google Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale and Sharon AI are exploring the software. In a proof of concept across NVIDIA HGX™ B200 systems with DSX MaxLPS, Lambda demonstrated 24% more cluster token throughput and 19% more GPU capacity within a fixed power budget. Coordinating AI Factory Power Demand With the Grid DSX Flex helps AI factories become flexible assets for the power grid, enabling operators to adapt workload power consumption to utility needs, demand-response events and energy prices. It can also coordinate electricity from the grid, onsite renewables and energy storage, helping AI factories operate as flexible power loads that support grid reliability and enable faster grid connection.  In an early trial, Emerald AI, EPRI, Nebius, the U.K. National Grid and NVIDIA demonstrated reductions of up to 40% in the cluster’s power draw on an NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPU cluster in response to simulated grid events, while critical workloads continued running. Nscale Advances AI Factory Efficiency With NVIDIA DSX Using DSX MaxLPS, DSX Flex and DSX Sim, Nscale is demonstrating how the NVIDIA DSX platform connects power optimization, grid-responsive operations and design. Based on an evaluation run in Nscale AI factory in Iceland, using DSX MaxLPS across four NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks, Nscale demonstrated 49% higher inference throughput and 37% more managed GPU capacity within the same 264-kilowatt provisioned power budget. The results demonstrate how dynamic power allocation can unlock additional capacity from existing infrastructure. Nscale is also exploring DSX Flex to align workload power consumption with grid conditions.  “Europe’s AI ambitions demand that we make every megawatt count,” said Josh Payne, founder and CEO of Nscale. “With NVIDIA DSX, we’re building AI factories that deliver more compute from available power, respond to grid conditions and move faster from design to deployment.” For its facilities in Portugal and Iceland, Nscale is using DSX Sim to create digital twins that help evaluate power, cooling and infrastructure configurations before deployment. events.title: NVIDIA Introduces DSX POD AI Factories to Accelerate Europe’s Infrastructure Deployment
events.summary: NVIDIA introduces DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners in modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. Factory-built units reduce deployment time at a prepared site from six months to as little as 14 days, helping customers begin generating production tokens and earning revenue sooner. A global ecosystem of computing and infrastructure partners are working with NVIDIA to deliver modular AI factories worldwide in early 2027. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today introduced DSX POD , a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. The units arrive ready to connect out of the box to a prepared site’s power, cooling, networking and other supporting infrastructure, reducing deployment time from six months to as little as 14 days. DSX POD moves the integration and installation of computing, networking, cabling, rack-level power and liquid cooling to the manufacturing facility, reducing the extensive planning, construction, specialized labor and logistics of a traditional onsite build. Factory-tested containers reduce exposure to component delays and costly, error-prone onsite work, creating a shorter path to model training and production inference so customers can begin generating tokens and earning revenue sooner. “An AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens — not when construction is complete,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA DSX POD, we’re bringing factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster.” Factory-Built Infrastructure NVIDIA DSX POD brings Vera Rubin systems together with the infrastructure needed to operate them in repeatable, factory-built, containerized designs that partners can manufacture and deliver at scale. It carries forward the design philosophy of the broader NVIDIA DSX™ infrastructure platform , with a distinct architecture that integrates and validates systems in purpose-built containers before transport and deployment. Partners complete rack-to-rack cabling, wiring, piping and functional validation before shipment. This work takes place separately from site preparation, further shortening the time needed to bring new capacity online. That earlier start to production is the link between deployment speed and economics. Time to first token marks when a new AI factory begins running models to serve production workloads, giving operators the opportunity to put their infrastructure to work for customers sooner. Global Partner Ecosystem and Availability NVIDIA is working with Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe , DayOne, Dell Technologies, Delta, Eaton, Foxconn (Ingrasys), GIGABYTE, HPE, Lenovo, Pegatron, Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT), Schneider Electric, Vertiv and Wistron to deliver DSX POD AI factories worldwide in early 2027.
